FROZEN CONTRACT: src/types/ is owned by the interface author. Do not edit or add files there; if something is missing, report it up rather than patching locally. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with these files in place (verified, plus a throwaway smoke file exercising DeviceDefinition.create, TransportDeps and descriptor construction).

IMPORT LAYOUT. Barrel: `import type { ParamHandle, TempoMap } from "../types";` and `import { PPQ } from "../types";`. Deep imports (`../types/params`) are equally valid. tsconfig has verbatimModuleSyntax — type imports MUST use `import type` or the build fails. Only four runtime values exist in the whole contract: PPQ (960), TICKS_PER_WHOLE_NOTE, DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS (25), DEFAULT_LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS (0.2). Do not redeclare them anywhere; src/time/ must import PPQ, not define it.

STRICTNESS. exactOptionalPropertyTypes is on, so every optional field in the contract is declared `?: T | undefined` — spread partial option objects freely. noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on: `io.inputs["sc"]` is `AudioNode | undefined`; noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature forces bracket access on Record types.

PARAM IDS (SS4). `chan:<ChannelId>/dev:<DeviceInstanceId>/<localId>`, `chan:<id>/vol`, `chan:<id>/pan`, `chan:<id>/send:<ChannelId>`. src/params/ owns the build/parse helpers for these strings — nobody else concatenates them. Descriptors inside DeviceDefinition.params carry the DEVICE-LOCAL id ("cutoff"); the harness rewrites it to the full path at registration. Values are always REAL units, never normalized; taper mapping (TaperMapping) is the only normalization boundary.

TIME (SS8). Ticks are always integers at PPQ=960; a 1/16 is 240. TempoMap.secondsAt(0) === 0, segments sorted, first at tick 0, ticksAt() rounds to an integer. Seconds are always on the BaseAudioContext.currentTime clock — never Date.now/performance.now.

DEVICES (SS7). DeviceHost.mount runs the lifecycle in one place: `prepare` (once per context, where a worklet calls addModule) -> `create(ctx, io)` -> register each descriptor -> connectParam. Devices connect INTO io.out and read FROM io.in; the harness owns those nodes and all wiring outside the device. create() takes BaseAudioContext — never assume AudioContext (offline export in M4 reuses it). Definitions returned via the harness's `deviceInstance(spec)` helper must satisfy CreateDeviceInstance/DeviceInstanceSpec; the harness may add optional spec keys later, devices must not depend on their absence.

TRANSPORT (SS12). Transport is built from TransportDeps and the exported factory must satisfy CreateTransport; the clip-backed source factory must satisfy CreateClipEventSource. NoteEvent has an allocation contract: a source may yield the SAME mutable object each iteration — consumers read fields before advancing and never retain it. NoteEventSource.eventsInRange(from, to) is half-open and yields non-decreasing ticks. DeviceInstance's note methods are optional; NoteTarget's are required — the demo/engine adapts an instrument to a NoteTarget at the wiring point. stop() sends allNotesOff(now + eps). Worker clock protocol is ClockCommand / ClockTickMessage (seq for drop detection). M3's automation sampler attaches via addWindowFiller, so the transport needs no dependency on it.

OWNERSHIP EXTRA: demo-app additionally owns src/main.tsx, index.html and e2e/ (the M0 audible proof is its end-to-end test). audio-boot keeps the existing createAudioContext()/PLACEHOLDER_WORKLET_URL surface in src/engine/context; other packages consume audio only as BaseAudioContext.

Builders reject empty segments and segments containing `/`.

**taper.ts** — the single normalization boundary. `toNormalized`/`fromNormalized`/`clampToDescriptor` + `taperMapping` satisfying the frozen `TaperMapping`. linear / log (geometric, 20 Hz–20 kHz midpoint = 632 Hz) / `{pow:k}` as `real = min + span·nᵏ`. `clampToDescriptor` is total (NaN/∞ → clamped default) and quantizes per kind: toggle snaps to endpoints, enum rounds into the label index range, stepped snaps to the grid without overshooting `max` (float dust rounded off). `assertTaperUsable` throws for `log` with `min ≤ 0` and non-finite/`≤0` pow.

**descriptors.ts / text.ts** — the `p.*` factories the plan references (`p.hz`, `p.db`, `p.ms`, `p.percent`, `p.semitones`, `p.pan`, `p.continuous`, `p.stepped`, `p.enum`, `p.toggle`), each with a sensible taper and total `toText`/`fromText` (`"1.2k"` → 1200, `"-6db"` → −6, `"-inf"` → min, `"50R"` → 0.5, enum labels case-insensitive). Unknown unit suffixes parse as `null` rather than silently ×1.

**handle.ts** — `ParamHandleImpl` implementing `ParamHandle` verbatim. Fast path A `bindAudioParam(p)` seeds the param immediately then de-zippers with `cancelScheduledValues → setValueAtTime(current) → linearRampToValueAtTime` over `smoothingMs` (`DEFAULT_SMOOTHING_MS = 15`; discrete kinds jump, and a repeated value is not re-pushed). Fast path B `bindMessage(fn)` pushes `(value, audioClockSeconds)`. Rebinding replaces the earlier binding; `unbind()` drops it. **The design rule is structurally enforced: the `AudioParam` enters `bindAudioParam` and no member ever returns it** (a test asserts it is unreachable from the handle's own surface). `setLive` clamps to real units and never touches the document; `commit()` promotes live→base and emits exactly one commit (a no-op gesture emits nothing).

**registry.ts** — `createParamRegistry(options)` returning `AppParamRegistry` (the frozen `ParamRegistry` plus additive members). Holds the §4 state machine *in the registry, never in the document*: `setAutomated(true/false)`, user-touch-during-playback → `overridden` (automation writes dropped while suspended), `hasOverrides()`, `reenableAutomation()`, `onOverridesChange` for the transport pill; freeing a param snaps live back to `base()`. Descriptors are validated at registration (empty id, non-finite/inverted bounds, missing toText/fromText, unusable taper, duplicate id) and copied. `unregisterWhere` drops a whole device's params.

**frame.ts** — injectable rAF coalescing: 50 `setLive` calls request exactly one frame and fire one `onChange` with the latest value; state changes and base moves also mark dirty (knob arc + ghost dot repaint). `flushChanges()` drains synchronously for tests and teardown.

1. **No `CreateParamRegistry` type**, unlike `CreateDeviceHost`/`CreateTransport`. I export `createParamRegistry(options?: ParamRegistryOptions): AppParamRegistry`; integration should call it once and pass it as the `ParamRegistry` argument to the device host.
2. **The handle has no clock, and `AudioParam` exposes no context.** `setLive(v, source)` carries no `when`, so an AudioParam ramp has no time base. - src/engine/transport/clock.ts — `Clock` seam: `createWorkerClock` (real), `createTimerClock` (fallback where `Worker` is absent — headless tests, offline render), `createDefaultClock`. Tracks dropped ticks from the `seq` gap.
- src/engine/transport/manualClock.ts — hand-driven `Clock` for deterministic headless tests and (M4) lockstep OfflineAudioContext rendering; can emit deliberate drops.
- src/engine/transport/clipEventSource.ts — `createClipEventSource: CreateClipEventSource`. Walks clips in tick order unrolling clip loops on the fly; half-open `[from,to)`, non-decreasing ticks, note-off before note-on on ties, notes cut at loop/clip boundaries, muted/degenerate notes dropped once at construction. Zero allocation per window/event: per-clip note orderings precomputed, binary-search seek, k-way merge over a small plan array, and a single preallocated event object + iterator + iterator-result objects reused (per the NoteEvent allocation contract).
- src/engine/transport/transport.ts — `createTransport: CreateTransport` (plus `createEngineTransport`). On each 25 ms tick it schedules to `ctx.currentTime + 0.20`, converting ticks→seconds through the TempoMap only (§8), so every noteOn/noteOff carries an exact audio-clock timestamp. Transport loop brace unrolled here by splitting the look-ahead window at `loop.end` and re-anchoring. `positionTicks()/positionSeconds()` map currentTime back through per-pass anchors kept in preallocated Float64Arrays (rAF-safe, allocation-free). `addWindowFiller` gets `fillWindow(horizonSeconds, fromTick, toTick)` per window for M3. Playback starts 5 ms ahead of currentTime so first-window timestamps stay in the future (the playhead therefore reads exactly 5 ms behind the wall clock — asserted in a test).

CONTRACT PROBLEMS FOUND (implemented against the contract as frozen; nothing in src/types was edited)
1. No way to reach the `recording` state: `Transport.state` is readonly and `play()` only produces "playing" — there is no `record()`/`setRecording()`. I added `record(fromTick?)` on an exported `EngineTransport extends Transport`; the object still satisfies `Transport`, and `createTransport` still satisfies `CreateTransport` exactly. Consider adding `record()` to the contract.
2. No clock injection seam: `TransportDeps` has no clock, so nothing headless (tests, and M4's OfflineAudioContext export in "fill-everything mode") can drive the scheduler deterministically. Added optional `clock` on an exported `EngineTransportDeps extends TransportDeps`, consumed only by `createEngineTransport`.
3. `NoteEventSource`'s doc comment claims it unrolls "the transport loop brace", but `CreateClipEventSource` receives only clips and never sees a `LoopRegion` — the brace is transport state. The brace is therefore unrolled in the transport; the doc comment is misleading, the signature is right.
4. `Transport.positionSeconds()` is ambiguous ("song position in audio-clock seconds"). I return song time in seconds (TempoMap frame, consistent with `positionTicks()` and non-monotonic across a loop wrap), not `ctx.currentTime`. Worth pinning down in the contract.
5. `NoteTarget` has no way to cancel already-scheduled events, so a `stop()` inside the 200 ms look-ahead would otherwise leave straggler note-ons sounding after `allNotesOff(now+ε)`. Workaround: the transport remembers scheduled-but-unsounded note-ons in a preallocated ring and, on stop/seek/tempo-change, releases each at its own onset (plus the spec's `allNotesOff(now+ε)`). A `cancelScheduled(fromSeconds)` on `NoteTarget` would be the clean fix; devices could then drop the ring.
6. `MidiClip.loop` semantics are unspecified for material before `loop.start`. I chose Live-like behaviour: the first pass plays `[0, loop.end)` (so pre-loop material is a one-shot intro), then `[loop.start, loop.end)` repeats until `length`; with `loop.start === 0` this is plain tiling. Documented at the top of clipEventSource.ts and covered by tests.

WIRING NOTES FOR THE INTEGRATION AGENT
`import { createTransport, createClipEventSource } from "../engine/transport"` (barrel at src/engine/transport/index.ts also exports the clock factories and `createManualClock`). The transport needs a `NoteTarget` per track from `resolveTarget`; a `DeviceInstance`'s note methods are optional, so the adapter belongs at the wiring point as the contract says. In the browser the default clock is the real Worker; nothing else is required.

findings.planSection: SS3 (the two write paths) / SS4 (design rule)
findings.description: The registry hands EVERY caller the widened handle, not the SS4 ParamHandle: `get` (registry.ts:194), `require` (:198) and `list` (:210) are all typed `RegistryParamHandle`, whose extra verbs are `setBase`, `setAutomated`, `reenableAutomation` and `unbind` (handle.ts:48-58). handle.ts:35-39 documents these as "What the registry (and only the registry) may additionally do to a handle", but nothing narrows them: any holder of the registry — the M1/M2 UI included — gets them. I substantiated the consequences with a probe (mounted `core.filter` on the fake context through `createDeviceHost`, then acted only through the public registry API): (a) `params.require('chan:c1/dev:d1/cutoff').setBase(1234)` moved the live BiquadFilter `frequency` to 1234 AND overwrote the committed base value while emitting NO `onCommit` event — a third write path into both the DSP and the document-mirror value that bypasses `setLive`+`commit`, so M1's command bus/undo history can never see it (SS3: "There are exactly two ways anything changes at runtime"); (b) `params.require(id).unbind()` from outside silently severed the device's fast path — the following `setLive(300,'user')` left the node stuck at 1234, with no error and no way to rebind, since only `DeviceInstance.connectParam` rebinds and the host calls it once at mount. That is a raw engine-mutating setter reachable past the sanctioned ParamHandle surface.

findings.planSection: SS7 / SS14
findings.description: Neither shipped device goes through the harness's device-authoring seam: `deviceInstance()`, `rampOutAndDisconnect`, and the `gainParams`/`scaledParams` binding rules (src/devices/harness/deviceInstance.ts, ~290 lines) have zero non-test callers — verified by grep. filter.ts and polySynth.ts hand-build `DeviceInstance` and reimplement the gain-ramped teardown in src/devices/core/ramp.ts, a near-duplicate of `rampOutAndDisconnect` (same 20 ms ramp + 30 ms slack constants, independently declared). Two divergent ways to write a device now exist, the SS14 "one file" playbook helper is validated only by its own unit tests, and a future author imitating filter.ts (the natural model, per SS14's "imitating one file") bypasses the harness's binding/teardown seam entirely.

findings.planSection: SS7 ("Nothing else in the app knows what a device does internally")
findings.description: The core-device barrel publishes device internals outside their definition: `FILTER_TYPES` and `filterTypeFromIndex` (line 9) are the filter's private enum-index→BiquadFilterType mapping, and `POLY_SYNTH_PROCESSOR_NAME` (line 12) is the synth's worklet processor identity. The sanctioned channel for enum choices is `ParamDescriptor.labels` on the registered handle (SS4), and a processor name is meaningful only inside `create`/`prepare`. Today only tests import them (src/demo/engine.test.ts:20), so no production leak exists yet — but the barrel invites exactly the out-of-band device knowledge SS7 forbids.

findings.planSection: SS3 / SS4 (M0 "Proves: params")
findings.description: The UI half of the sanctioned bridge is never crossed in the assembled app. `createDemoEngine` builds the `ParamRegistry` internally and `DemoEngine` (engine.ts:53-57) exposes only `transport` and `dispose`, so App.tsx has no path to any `ParamHandle`; a grep for `setLive`/`commit()` across non-test src finds no production caller at all (the only handle read is `releaseHandle?.live()` in polySynth.ts:93). Fast path A is proven end to end only in the bind-time default push and in unit tests — the gesture→`setLive`→AudioParam→`commit` round trip the spine exists for is unexercised by the shipped app.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling — "unrolling clip loops and the transport loop brace on the fly")
findings.description: The transport loop brace is unrolled by truncating the look-ahead window at `loop.end` (transport.ts:304-315: `windowEnd = loop.end; wraps = true;` then `cursorTick = loop.start`), but nothing ever closes notes that are still sounding at the brace. `NoteEventSource.eventsInRange(from, to)` is half-open, so any note-off landing AT or AFTER `loop.end` is never emitted, and the next pass re-emits the note-on. `clipEventSource` deliberately clamps note-offs to the *clip*'s repetition end (`clamped = raw < contentEnd ? raw : contentEnd`) but the transport brace gets no equivalent cut, and its own header comment states the brace split "is the transport's job". Substantiated with a throwaway probe against the real transport (fixed 120bpm, ManualClock, loop {0, 2*PPQ}): (a) clip length 2 beats with notes 60@[0,960) and 64@[960,1920) — the emitted stream is `on 60 / off 60 / on 64 / on 60 / off 60 / on 64 / on 60 ...`: pitch 64 (the last note of the loop, ending exactly on the brace — the typical case) gets a note-on every pass and NEVER a note-off, so it sustains at the ADSR sustain level for the whole loop and is only silenced by `stop()`'s allNotesOff; (b) a note spanning the brace (start 0, dur 1 bar, brace at 2 beats) yields `on 60 @0.005 / on 60 @1.005 / on 60 @2.005 / ...` with zero note-offs. Existing loop unit tests only use notes that both start and end strictly inside the brace, so this is untested.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling — "Stop sends allNotesOff(now + ε) down every track")
findings.description: `stop()` does not actually silence the instrument for notes already handed to it inside the 200 ms look-ahead window. `panic()` (transport.ts:325-340) sends `allNotesOff(now+5ms)` and, for each still-future pending note-on, a `noteOff(onsetTime + 5ms)` — the comment claims this means it "never becomes an audible straggler", but the note-on itself was already posted to the worklet and cannot be retracted: `PolySynthProcessor.applyEvent` for `allNotesOff` only releases *currently sounding* voices and leaves later-timestamped events sitting in `NoteEventQueue.pending`, so the queued note-on still fires after Stop. With the shipped device defaults (attack 5 ms, release 250 ms) a note-on followed by a note-off 5 ms later reaches full amplitude 1.0 and then rings ~247 ms — verified by driving `AdsrEnvelope` directly. Probe on the real demo clip: play from 0, stop at ctx.currentTime = 0.35 s → panic emits `noteOff 67 @0.5100` for a note-on already scheduled at 0.505 s, i.e. an audible full-amplitude blip ~155 ms AFTER Stop plus its release tail (~0.4 s of sound after the button press). The e2e check (e2e/interaction/audio-graph.spec.ts) hides this: it polls for RMS < 0.01 with a 500 ms timeout instead of requiring silence within the ~5 ms epsilon the spec implies.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Guardrails — "zero allocation in per-tick paths (preallocated event objects, ring buffers for messages)")
findings.description: The transport honours the zero-allocation guardrail meticulously (preallocated `NoteEvent`, typed-array anchor/pending rings, index loops), and then the instrument's message path breaks it in both directions. (1) Main thread, inside the per-tick scheduling loop: `PolySynth.noteOn/noteOff/allNotesOff` (src/devices/core/polySynth.ts:76-82) allocate a fresh object literal per note event (`post({ type: "noteOn", pitch, vel, when })`) which is then structured-cloned — exactly the "ring buffer for messages" the plan calls for is absent. (2) Audio render thread, every render quantum: `process()` calls `this.queue.popDue(...)` (poly-synth-processor.ts:87), and `NoteEventQueue.popDue` unconditionally allocates two arrays (`due`, `remaining`) plus one `{event, offset}` wrapper per due event and runs `Array.prototype.sort` — ~690 array allocations/second at 44.1 kHz/128 even when no events are pending; the per-sample loops additionally use `for (const voice of this.voices)` and `for (const channel of output)` (lines 94, 104), i.e. iterator allocation inside the innermost sample loop. GC pressure on the audio thread is precisely the failure this guardrail exists to prevent.

findings.planSection: SS12 ("Note events call instrument.noteOn(pitch, vel, when) with exact context timestamps, so jitter in the tick loop never reaches the audio")
findings.description: The exact audio-clock timestamp the scheduler works hard to compute is discarded inside the instrument. `NoteEventQueue.popDue` computes a sample-accurate `offset` via `sampleOffsetForBlock` (which is itself documented and unit-tested as "pure sample-accurate scheduling math"), but `process()` (lines 87-90) ignores `offset` entirely and applies every due event at the start of the render quantum: `for (const { event } of due) this.applyEvent(event, ...)`. Note onsets are therefore quantized to 128-sample boundaries (~2.9 ms at 44.1 kHz) with the quantization error varying per note depending on block phase — i.e. up to ~2.9 ms of timing jitter reintroduced at the last hop, in the one place the plan singles out as the reason for the two-clock design.

findings.planSection: SS14 (Extensibility playbook — helper library `p.*`)
findings.description: The §14 descriptor factories diverge from the playbook in two ways that a device author following the plan will hit. (a) Option key: the plan's one-file delay is written `p.time('timeL','Time L',{ min:1, max:2000, defaultValue:250 })` / `p.pct('mix','Mix',{ defaultValue:25 })`, but `RangeOptions` requires `default` and rejects `defaultValue` (excess property under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` + missing required member) — so the §14 snippet does not compile as written; the claim in src/devices/harness/params.ts's header that "`p.pct('mix','Mix',{ default:25 })` from the SS14 stereo-delay example compiles verbatim" quietly restates the example rather than matching it. (b) Two different `p` objects exist: `src/params/descriptors.ts` exports `percent`/`semitones` with no `pct`/`st`/`time`, while the §14 spellings live only on the harness re-export (`src/devices/harness/params.ts`). Both shipped device definitions (src/devices/core/filter.ts, polySynth.ts) import `p` from `../../params/descriptors`, i.e. from the package where `p.pct`, `p.st` and `p.time` do not exist — so a new device author copying the playbook into `src/devices/core/` gets a type error on the plan's own names.

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport & scheduling — "Stop sends allNotesOff(now + ε) down every track"); §18 M0
findings.description:
Stop does not silence the instrument: note-ons already posted into the worklet inside the 200 ms look-ahead still fire AFTER the transport has stopped, as full-amplitude ghost notes.

Mechanism: the worklet protocol has only noteOn/noteOff/allNotesOff (polySynth.ts:75-83; poly-synth-processor.ts:64-66, 111-139) — there is no cancel/flush message, and `NoteEventQueue.pending` (noteEventQueue.ts:22) is never purged. `transport.stop()` -> `panic()` (transport.ts:325-343) therefore cannot retract the queued note-ons; it compensates by posting `noteOff(pitch, pendingTime + 5 ms)`. With the synth's default attack of 5 ms (polySynth.ts:35) that note-on still reaches full level before its note-off lands, and then decays over the 250 ms default release (polySynth.ts:37). `seek()` (transport.ts:434-445) and `setTempoMap()` take the same path.

Substantiated in headless Chromium against the production build (Playwright probe tapping ctx.destination with an AnalyserNode, same technique as e2e/interaction/audio-graph.spec.ts). RMS sampled every ~20 ms from the instant the Stop button is clicked, two consecutive runs:
  t=0ms 0.425 | 38ms 0.413 | 58ms 0.505 | 78ms 0.571 | 99ms 0.543 | 139ms 0.437 | 238ms 0.189 | 319ms 0.013 | 340ms 0.000
Level RISES ~35% above the level at Stop (0.42 -> 0.57 at +78 ms) — a decaying tail cannot rise, so that is a new note attacking after Stop — and audio persists ~330 ms past the button press.

Not caught by e2e/interaction/audio-graph.spec.ts:191-201, which only polls (up to 500 ms) until RMS drops below 0.01, so it tolerates exactly this artifact. Fix needs a cancel-scheduled-events message the worklet honours (drop every queued event with when >= t), not a compensating noteOff.

findings.planSection: §12 (Guardrails — "zero allocation in per-tick paths (preallocated event objects, ring buffers for messages)"); §2 (Performance budgets)
findings.description:
The audio-rendering thread allocates on every render quantum, so the guardrail holds on the scheduler tick path but is violated where it matters most.

`NoteEventQueue.popDue()` (noteEventQueue.ts:38-52) is called once per `process()` call (poly-synth-processor.ts:87) and unconditionally allocates two arrays (`due`, `remaining`), replaces `this.pending` with the new array, allocates a `{event, offset}` wrapper per due event, and allocates a comparator closure for `due.sort()` — regardless of whether anything is due. That is ~375 calls/second/instrument at 48 kHz / 128. On top of it, `process()` allocates an ADSR options object per due event (`this.applyEvent(event, { attackMs, decayMs, sustainPct, releaseMs })`, poly-synth-processor.ts:89), `AdsrEnvelope.noteOn` receives a second fresh object literal (poly-synth-processor.ts:121-126), and `VoiceAllocator.releaseAll()` allocates an array on every allNotesOff (voiceAllocator.ts:48-56).

Measured (node, importing the real module, one instrument, queue holding a single future note so nothing is ever due): 22,500 `popDue` calls = 60 s of audio triggered 4 GC events (3.3 ms total) from `popDue` alone. At the §2 budget of ~16 tracks that is ~64 scavenges/minute on the audio thread, each competing with a 2.67 ms render-quantum deadline, plus the per-event garbage during actual playback. §12 names the intended shape explicitly — "ring buffers for messages" — and none of the message path uses one. Note the contrast: the scheduler side (clipEventSource.ts, transport.ts, clock.worker.ts) is genuinely allocation-free, and there is no test anywhere asserting the worklet side is.

findings.planSection: §7 (Device system — "Removal is the reverse, gain-ramped"; swap semantics step 3, "~20 ms crossfade; old disposed after its tail")
findings.description:
Instrument teardown is not click-free: the harness cuts the instrument's audio ~260 ms before the instrument thinks its tail has finished, and the instrument never ramps its own gain at all.

host.ts:123-141 disposes a mounted device by calling `instance.dispose(when)` and then scheduling `bundle.dispose()` — which hard-`disconnect()`s every harness-owned port GainNode (io.ts:107-111) — at `teardownRampMs * 2` = 40 ms (DEFAULT_RAMP_OUT_MS = 20, deviceInstance.ts:23). The comment there claims "The ports outlive the instance's own fade by design", but `PolySynth.dispose` (polySynth.ts:87-98) posts `allNotesOff` and then relies on the envelope's release — default 250 ms — disconnecting its own node only at `releaseMs + 50` ≈ 300 ms. The port node is therefore disconnected at 40 ms, mid-release, while the envelope is still at a high level (a 250 ms linear release is at ~0.84 of peak after 40 ms): a step discontinuity, i.e. a click, on every instrument unmount/swap and on `engine.dispose()`.

Unlike `core.filter`, which fades through `rampAndDisconnect` (filter.ts:74, ramp.ts:30-50), the poly synth performs no gain ramp whatsoever — it has no owned output gain — so nothing in the chain smooths that cut. `deviceInstance.ts` even documents 20 ms as "the harness's default ramp" per §7, but the two timelines (fixed 40 ms harness wait vs. release-derived 300 ms device wait) are never reconciled.

Compounded by the missing cancel path (finding 1): a note-on queued in the worklet can fire after `allNotesOff` and then be hard-disconnected mid-note.

findings.planSection: §12 ("Note events call instrument.noteOn(pitch, vel, when) with exact context timestamps, so jitter in the tick loop never reaches the audio")
findings.description: Sample-accurate placement is computed and then thrown away. `sampleOffsetForBlock` (polySynth/scheduling.ts) computes each event's exact sample index inside the current render quantum, `popDue` sorts by it and returns it as `DueNoteEvent.offset` (noteEventQueue.ts:15-19), but `process()` destructures only the event — `for (const { event } of due) this.applyEvent(...)` (poly-synth-processor.ts:88-90) — and applies every due event at sample 0, before the sample loop begins. Every note is therefore quantized to the 128-sample block grid (up to 2.67 ms early at 48 kHz) and all notes falling in one block collapse onto the same instant, defeating the exact `when` the scheduler went to some trouble to compute. The file's own header ("`NoteEventQueue` holds them until `sampleOffsetForBlock` says they belong to the block currently rendering") and scheduling.ts's header ("Pure sample-accurate scheduling math") describe behaviour the processor does not implement. The fix is to split the sample loop at each event offset.

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport & scheduling — look-ahead scheduler)
findings.description: A main-thread stall longer than the look-ahead degrades into an event burst rather than a resync. `onTick` (transport.ts:286-321) advances `cursorTime` purely by accumulated musical duration and never clamps it to `ctx.currentTime`. If the main thread is blocked for longer than `lookAhead` (200 ms) — plausible once M1's canvas editors, project load, or GC land on this thread — the next tick schedules the whole backlog in one pass, handing the instrument events whose `when` is already in the past. `sampleOffsetForBlock` clamps every past `when` to offset 0 (polySynth/scheduling.ts:22), so the entire backlog fires simultaneously in one render quantum (a chord of what should have been a sequence, and up to MAX_VOICES worth of voice-stealing), after which playback stays permanently late by the stall duration with no recovery path. Worth an explicit policy — drop/compress the backlog, or re-anchor `cursorTime`/`cursorTick` to `now` — since §12's design intent is that scheduler jitter "never reaches the audio".

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport & scheduling — "unrolling clip loops and the transport loop brace on the fly")
findings.description:
Off-by-one at the loop-brace boundary permanently disables the transport loop. In onTick() (line 305) the wrap only fires when `windowEnd > loop.end`; when the look-ahead boundary lands *exactly* on loop.end (`windowEnd === loop.end`, which is a normal outcome because `tempoMap.ticksAt()` rounds to the nearest integer tick) `wraps` stays false and `cursorTick` is set to `loop.end`. On every later pass the guard `cursorTick < loop.end` is now false, so the brace is never applied again and the transport plays straight on past it forever — the loop is silently gone until stop/seek.

Substantiated with a throwaway vitest probe using the repo's own ManualClock rig: (a) contrived — 120 bpm, lookAhead 0.2 s, START_LEAD 0.005 s makes the first boundary land at tick round(0.195*1920)=374, so `loop {start:0,end:374,enabled:true}` yields exactly 1 note-on inside the brace and then schedules a note at tick 1000 (`{kind:"on",pitch:90,when:0.5258…}`) that lies past loop.end; (b) realistic — a 1-bar brace `{0, 3840}` at 120 bpm with jittery tick arrival (20–30 ms) escaped the brace in 42 of 60 trials within 60 loop passes. Instrumenting `ticksAt` confirms the trigger every time: the window-end sequence steps ~48 ticks per tick, and the pass where it returns exactly 3840 is the pass where playback continues to 3895, 3942, … . Probability ≈1/48 per loop cycle, i.e. an ordinary 1-bar loop breaks after ~1.5 minutes of looped playback. The existing loop tests (transport.test.ts:295-354) never hit the exact-equality case.

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport & scheduling — event iterator unrolls the transport loop brace; noteOn/noteOff pairing)
findings.description:
A note sustaining across the transport loop brace is never released — a permanently stuck voice. The clip-loop unroller in clipEventSource.ts deliberately clamps note-offs at every repetition boundary (`const clamped = raw < p.contentEnd ? raw : p.contentEnd`), but the brace unroller in transport.ts (lines 305-320) just truncates the window at `loop.end` and jumps `cursorTick` to `loop.start`; nothing emits note-offs for pitches still held at the brace, and their real note-off tick is never scheduled because playback never reaches it.

Probe: clip length 4 bars with one note `{start: 5760, dur: 3840, pitch: 60}` (spanning ticks 5760-9600) and loop `{start:0, end:7680, enabled:true}` at 120 bpm produces the call sequence `[on@3.005, on@7.005, on@11.005]` — three note-ons, zero note-offs. In the poly synth the allocator retriggers the same voice each pass and the envelope stays in sustain forever; only stop()/allNotesOff silences it.

findings.planSection: §12 ("Note events call instrument.noteOn(pitch, vel, when) with exact context timestamps")
findings.description:
The computed sample offset is discarded, so note events are not sample-accurate and short notes are dropped entirely. Line 87-90: `const due = this.queue.popDue(currentTime, sampleRate, blockSize); for (const { event } of due) this.applyEvent(...)` — `DueNoteEvent.offset` (documented "Sample index within the current block", computed and sorted on by NoteEventQueue/sampleOffsetForBlock, whose header calls itself "Pure sample-accurate scheduling math") is destructured away and every due event is applied at the block start. Consequences: (1) all note timing quantizes to the 128-sample render quantum (~2.7 ms at 48 kHz), which is the jitter §12's two-clock design exists to avoid; (2) a noteOn/noteOff pair that falls inside one block collapses to zero length and the note is completely silent — AdsrEnvelope.noteOn sets stage='attack' at level 0, the immediately-following noteOff computes `releaseInc = 0/(release*sr) = 0` and `next()` then drops it straight to idle.

Probe reproducing the processor's exact loop: pushing `noteOn(when=0.0002)` and `noteOff(when=0.0007)` yields `due = [{noteOn, offset:10},{noteOff, offset:34}]`, and applying it the way the processor does gives peak amplitude 0 over 40 blocks, stage 'idle'. Any note shorter than ~2.7 ms (≥5 ticks at 120 bpm; the type contract only requires `dur >= 1`) is silently lost.

findings.planSection: §12 ("Stop sends allNotesOff(now + ε) down every track")
findings.description:
stop() leaves audible ghost notes from the look-ahead window. panic() (lines 327-336) cannot retract note-ons already handed to the instrument, so for each pending note-on it schedules `noteOff(pitch, pendingTime + STOP_EPSILON_SECONDS)` — i.e. 5 ms *after* the note's own onset — while `allNotesOff(now + ε)` only releases voices sounding at that instant. The synth's `allNotesOff` handler (poly-synth-processor.ts applyEvent → allocator.releaseAll) does not purge queued future events from NoteEventQueue, so the queued note-on still fires up to `lookAhead` (200 ms) after the user pressed stop, runs a full 5 ms attack (the default attack is exactly 5 ms, so it reaches full amplitude) and then rings out its 250 ms release.

Probe: play from tick 0, tick at ctx.currentTime = 0.10, then stop() — the recorded calls contain `{kind:"on",pitch:61,when:0.255}` and `{kind:"off",pitch:61,when:0.26}`, i.e. a full-amplitude note starting 155 ms after stop. The existing test "releases note-ons that were already scheduled inside the horizon" (transport.test.ts:419) asserts this behaviour rather than catching it.

findings.planSection: §7 (Device system — instrument voice allocation behind noteOn/noteOff/allNotesOff)
findings.description:
Voice stealing frees a voice on note-off while its release tail is still sounding, and `allocate()` then picks the *lowest-index* free slot (line 31, `this.pitches.indexOf(null)`), so a monophonic melody reuses voice 0 for every note and each note truncates its predecessor's release. The allocator has no notion of envelope state (release() nulls the slot immediately; AdsrEnvelope.noteOn deliberately ramps from the current level rather than resetting) and the free-slot search is index-order rather than least-recently-used, so idle voices are never preferred over still-ringing released ones.

Probe with the actual demo phrase (src/demo/clip.ts: 8 eighth notes, dur 440 ticks, 40-tick gap, default release 250 ms): `allocate/release` per note returns voice indices `[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]`. Every note's 250 ms release is cut ~21 ms in by the next note retriggering the same voice, so the 8-voice "poly synth" never overlaps two release tails.

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport states)
findings.description: stop-while-starting re-entrancy leaves the clock running. beginPlayback (lines 355-362) does `setState(next); onTick(); clock.start(tickIntervalMs);` — state listeners are invoked synchronously inside setState, so a listener that calls transport.stop() runs `clock.stop()` *before* `clock.start()` is reached. Probe: `transport.onStateChange(s => { if (s === 'playing') transport.stop(); }); transport.play(0);` ends with `state: stopped, clock.running: true` — a 40 Hz worker/timer tick that runs forever (onTick early-returns while stopped) until dispose().

findings.planSection: §12 (Guardrails — context boot/unlock) / §18 M0 "Context boot + unlock"
findings.description: Double-start race on boot. handleBoot's re-entrancy guard is `if (engineRef.current) return;` (line 32) but `engineRef.current` is only assigned after two awaits (`bootAudioContext` and `createDemoEngine`), and the button's only disable condition is `disabled={ready}`, which is likewise set at the end. Two quick clicks therefore run two full boots: two AudioContexts, two worklet module loads, two synth→filter chains, and two unlock listener sets (bootAudioContext also discards the Unsub returned by unlockAudioContextOnGesture). The first engine/context is overwritten in the ref and never disposed or closed, so it keeps the audio hardware alive; repeating this exhausts the browser's per-page AudioContext limit.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing: "no browser needed for any of the load-bearing logic")
findings.description:
The entire `PolySynthProcessor` class — the M0 instrument's actual audio-thread logic: per-block dispatch of due note events, voice allocation -> envelope wiring, velocity scaling, per-sample oscillator mix, phase accumulation, one-pole filter, dB->linear gain, channel write — has ZERO tests. Grep confirms no test file imports `src/worklets/poly-synth-processor.ts` (the only references are prose comments plus `e2e/render/worklet-chunk.spec.ts`, which only checks that a chunk with that filename is served with a 200). `polySynth.test.ts` (11 tests) covers only the MAIN-THREAD definition (node construction, param binding, port messages, dispose); the `polySynth/*` leaf modules (envelope, oscillator, voiceAllocator, noteEventQueue, scheduling, onePoleLowpass) are each tested in isolation, but the class that composes them is not. The file's own header claims the DSP "stays unit-testable head-on in plain Vitest (SS15)" — that is true of the leaves only, and the composition is where the bugs live.

Substantiated, not speculative: I loaded the module in plain Vitest from the scratchpad with ~10 lines of stubs (`vi.stubGlobal` for `AudioWorkletProcessor`, `sampleRate`, `currentTime`, `registerProcessor`) and drove `process()` directly, so the gap is a choice, not a technical impossibility. That 15-line probe immediately caught a real defect no existing test can see: line 87 computes `this.queue.popDue(currentTime, sampleRate, blockSize)`, whose `DueNoteEvent.offset` is the sample index within the block, but line 88 destructures `for (const { event } of due)` and throws the offset away — every event in a block is applied at the block boundary. Consequence I measured: a noteOn at sample 10 and its noteOff at sample 34 of the SAME 128-sample quantum both apply before rendering, so the voice's envelope is released before a single sample is produced — peak amplitude 0 over 40 blocks (a long note in the identical rig renders fine, so the rig is valid). `NoteEventQueue.popDue`'s offsets are thoroughly unit-tested ("returns due events ordered by sample offset") while nothing asserts any consumer uses them. Neither browser test can see this: `e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts` analyses 50 ms RMS windows of 250 ms notes, and `e2e/interaction/audio-graph.spec.ts` samples RMS every few hundred ms. Report only — I did not add the test or fix the offset handling.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) / SS4 (registry owns the one range truth)
findings.description: The synth's param ranges are duplicated across a package boundary with nothing pinning them together: `parameterDescriptors` (lines 40-49) hard-codes cutoff 40..18000, attack/decay 1..4000, sustain 0..100, release 1..6000, gain -60..6, and `src/devices/core/polySynth.ts` lines 32-38 re-declares the same numbers via `p.*`. They happen to agree today (I diffed them by hand), but no test asserts it. `polySynth.test.ts` already sets the precedent for exactly this kind of cross-boundary pin — "shape's labels are exactly the worklet's OSCILLATOR_SHAPES, in order" — and simply stops at labels. A later widening of a descriptor range (very likely in M4's device work) would be silently clamped by the worklet-side `AudioParam` min/max, producing an automation ceiling with no failing test anywhere.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) / SS12 (look-ahead scheduler)
findings.description: The single OfflineAudioContext integration test exists and passes (`npx playwright test e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts` -> 1 passed), but it renders with `lookAheadSeconds: durationSeconds` and a `ManualClock` that is never ticked, so `beginPlayback` schedules the whole clip in ONE window before `startRendering()`. SS12's actual runtime regime — successive look-ahead windows posting note messages into the worklet's `NoteEventQueue` while rendering is already under way — is therefore never exercised against a real audio graph offline; it is covered only by `e2e/interaction/audio-graph.spec.ts`'s coarse realtime RMS sampling, whose resolution is hundreds of milliseconds. `OfflineAudioContext.suspend(time)/resume()` would let the same render advance in windows and tick the clock between them, which is what would make the offline test a real proof of the scheduler-to-worklet handoff rather than of a degenerate single-window case.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing)
findings.description: `npx vitest run` is currently RED: 5 failures across `src/engine/transport/__probe.test.ts`, `__probe2.test.ts`, `__probe5.test.ts` and `src/devices/core/polySynth/__probe6.test.ts`, so `npm test` — the milestone's own unit-test command — exits non-zero. Attribution matters here: these files' mtimes are 19:50-19:55, i.e. they were written DURING this review round by parallel review agents dropping throwaway probes into `src/` instead of a scratchpad, and they match vite.config.ts's include glob `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`. They are not the implementer's code and their assertions are probe hypotheses (at least `__probe2`'s "ghost note-on" claim is wrong — `transport.ts` deliberately emits a note-off at onset+epsilon for horizon-committed note-ons, which `transport.test.ts:419` already covers). The actionable point for the gate is hygiene: the tree must be swept of `src/**/__probe*.test.ts` before acceptance, since anything left behind keeps the suite red. Excluding those files, all 33 remaining unit test files (297 tests) pass, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, and all 11 Playwright specs pass.

fixed: BLOCKER loop brace off-by-one (src/engine/transport/transport.ts): the wrap guard is now `windowEnd >= loop.end` (was `>`), so a look-ahead boundary landing exactly on the brace (ordinary, since tempoMap.ticksAt rounds) still wraps instead of parking cursorTick on loop.end and losing the loop forever. Regression test added in transport.test.ts ('wraps when the window boundary lands exactly on loop.end'); verified it FAILS against the old `>` and passes after.

Notes held across the loop brace are now released (src/engine/transport/transport.ts): a preallocated sounding-note ring (markSounding/clearSounding, typed arrays, zero allocation per S12) tracks note-ons with no scheduled note-off; on a wrap cutSounding(endTime) emits noteOff at the brace before cursorTick jumps back - the same cut clipEventSource applies at clip repetition boundaries. Reset on play/seek/panic; ring overflow falls back to allNotesOff at the brace. Test: 'cuts a note held across the brace and re-triggers it on the next pass'.

Stop now actually silences the instrument (src/devices/core/polySynth/noteEventQueue.ts): allNotesOff is a cancel as well as a release - pushing it drops every queued event with when >= its timestamp, at push time (not apply time, so a seek's freshly scheduled window pushed afterwards is untouched). The 200 ms of look-ahead note-ons already inside the worklet can no longer attack after Stop. The transport's compensating noteOff(onset+eps) is kept as a fallback for note targets without cancel semantics. Tests: noteEventQueue.test.ts cancel cases, poly-synth-processor.test.ts 'allNotesOff silences notes the look-ahead already queued', and e2e/interaction/audio-graph.spec.ts now samples RMS every 25 ms for 250 ms after Stop and fails if the level RISES (a decaying tail cannot rise, so a climb is a ghost note attacking).

Sample-accurate note placement restored (src/worklets/poly-synth-processor.ts): process() splits its sample loop at each due event's offset instead of applying every due event at the block boundary. Notes now start on their own sample, and a noteOn/noteOff pair inside one 128-sample quantum no longer collapses to silence. Tests: 'starts a note on its own sample, not on the block boundary' and 'a note shorter than one render quantum still sounds'.

Zero-allocation guardrail (S12) now holds on the audio thread. NoteEventQueue is a preallocated ring: incoming message fields are copied into Int8/Int32/Float32/Float64 arrays, collectDue() sorts in place (stable insertion sort) into a second preallocated due buffer and returns a count - no arrays, wrapper objects, closures or Array.sort per render quantum. The processor's ADSR config object is preallocated and reused; every for...of over voices/channels is now an index loop; VoiceAllocator.releaseAll() (allocated an array per panic) is replaced by clear(). Queue and allocator tests updated to the new API.

Registry no longer hands the widened handle to every caller (src/params/registry.ts, src/params/handle.ts): get/require/list now return the S4 ParamHandle (the frozen contract's own type), as does unregisterWhere's predicate and ParamCommit.handle. setBase/setAutomated/reenableAutomation/unbind reach only the caller that registered the param, so no third write path into the DSP is reachable past setLive+commit. registry.test.ts pins this with @ts-expect-error assertions (enforced by tsc).

Instrument teardown is click-free (src/devices/core/polySynth.ts): the synth now owns an output GainNode and disposes through rampOutAndDisconnect - a 20 ms fade reaching zero well before the harness disconnects its port nodes at 2x its 20 ms ramp, instead of the old release-derived ~300 ms wait that left the worklet ringing when the ports were cut at 40 ms. Test: 'dispose sends allNotesOff, fades its own gain, then disconnects'.

Voice allocation is least-recently-used, not lowest-index (src/devices/core/polySynth/voiceAllocator.ts): release() keeps the slot's last-use stamp and allocate() picks the LRU free voice (never-used slots first), so a monophonic melody walks the pool instead of retriggering voice 0 and truncating every 250 ms release tail. Tests: 'spreads a monophonic melody across the pool' and 'prefers a never-used voice over a recently released one'.

PolySynthProcessor now has tests (src/worklets/poly-synth-processor.test.ts, 10 cases): the class is exported and driven head-on in plain Vitest with the four worklet globals stubbed - silence, scheduled note, sample-offset placement, sub-quantum note, allNotesOff cancel and release, polyphony, velocity scaling, and registration name.

Worklet parameterDescriptors are pinned to the device descriptors (same test file, 'keeps its AudioParam ranges identical to the device descriptors'): min/max/default for every shared id are compared against PolySynth.params, so a widened descriptor can no longer be silently clamped by a stale AudioParam range across the postMessage boundary.

S14 playbook spellings now compile verbatim (src/params/descriptors.ts): p.pct / p.st / p.time live next to the factories they alias (so src/devices/core/*, which imports p from ../../params/descriptors, gets the plan's own names), and every factory accepts `defaultValue:` as well as `default:` via a DefaultOption union that still requires exactly one. src/devices/harness/params.ts is now a plain re-export, so there is one p in the codebase. Test: 'builds the stereo-delay params exactly as S14 writes them'.

Both shipped devices now go through the S14 authoring seam (src/devices/core/filter.ts, polySynth.ts): they build their DeviceInstance with deviceInstance({audioParams, messageParams, note methods, dispose}) and tear down with rampOutAndDisconnect. The duplicate src/devices/core/ramp.ts (and its test) is deleted, so the ~20 ms ramp + 30 ms slack constants exist once and the file a future author imitates is the seam the playbook advertises. No cycle: the harness does not import core.

Core device barrel no longer publishes device internals (src/devices/core/index.ts): FILTER_TYPES, filterTypeFromIndex, FilterType and POLY_SYNTH_PROCESSOR_NAME are gone from it (S7); src/demo/engine.test.ts imports the processor name from its own module.

The param bridge is now crossed by the shipped app (src/demo/engine.ts, src/app/App.tsx): DemoEngine exposes params (lookups hand back ParamHandle only) plus DEMO_CUTOFF_PARAM_ID, and App renders a live filter-cutoff slider that does taper-mapped setLive on drag and commit on release - fast path A end to end. Test: engine.test.ts 'drives the live filter through the S4 handle, and commits once' asserts the drag reaches the BiquadFilter without emitting a commit, then exactly one commit with the right previous value.

Main-thread stall policy (src/engine/transport/transport.ts): when cursorTime has fallen behind ctx.currentTime, onTick closes the current anchor and re-anchors at now + START_LEAD instead of dumping the backlog, so no batch of already-past timestamps is ever handed to an instrument (which sampleOffsetForBlock would collapse into one render quantum). Test: 're-anchors instead of dumping a backlog of past timestamps'.

Stop-while-starting re-entrancy (src/engine/transport/transport.ts): beginPlayback re-checks the state after setState and after the first onTick, so a listener that calls stop() from the state callback no longer leaves a 40 Hz clock running forever. Test: 'a listener that stops the transport during play() leaves no clock running'.

Double-boot race (src/app/App.tsx): a synchronous bootingRef guard plus disabled={ready || booting} - two fast clicks can no longer create two AudioContexts, two worklet loads and two chains with the first orphaned.

Offline render now exercises the real look-ahead regime (src/demo/offlineRender.ts): default 200 ms look-ahead with OfflineAudioContext.suspend/resume at render-quantum-aligned 25 ms steps ticking the ManualClock mid-render, instead of one fill-everything window before startRendering. The result reports ticks, and e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts asserts ticks > 10 so the scheduler-to-worklet handoff is actually proven.

Playwright webServer failures are diagnosable (playwright.config.ts): stdout/stderr are piped, so the tsc error behind 'Process from config.webServer was not able to start. Exit code: 2' is visible without DEBUG=pw:webserver. The pre-build typecheck itself is left in place deliberately.

findings.planSection: §3 (the two write paths) / §4 (design rule)
findings.description: `DemoEngine.params` is typed `AppParamRegistry`, not the frozen `ParamRegistry`, so the UI layer (`src/app/App.tsx` holds the engine in `engineRef`) is handed `load()`, `register()`, `unregisterWhere()`, `setClock()` and `dispose()` in addition to `get`/`require`. `AppParamRegistry.load({id: v})` calls `ParamHandleImpl.setBase`, which for a `free` param falls through to `#writeLive` → the bound `AudioParam` — a write into the DSP that bypasses `setLive`+`commit` and is invisible to `onCommit`. That is precisely the 'third write path' the doc comment in `src/params/registry.ts` (lines ~55-65) claims the seam prevents ('would be a third write path into the DSP … invisible to `onCommit`'). Nothing misuses it in M0, so this is surface, not a live bug: narrowing `DemoEngine.params` to `ParamRegistry` (or a UI-facing subset) would close it.

findings.planSection: §3 (unidirectional core; the registry is the one sanctioned bridge)
findings.description: The e2e bridge is unconditional, not dev/test-gated: `window.__fabletonDemo = bridge` plus `onEngineReady={(engine) => { bridge.engine = engine; }}` ships in the production build — confirmed by `grep -rl "__fabletonDemo" dist` hitting `dist/assets/index-BZlhFW9X.js`. Any script on the page therefore gets the live `AppParamRegistry` (including `load`/`register`/`unregisterWhere`/`dispose`) and the full `EngineTransport` (`setTempoMap`, `addWindowFiller`, `record`, `dispose`), i.e. an out-of-band route around the command/handle seam in the shipped app. Gating the assignment behind `import.meta.env.DEV` (or a Playwright-only flag) keeps the e2e proof without the production hole.

findings.planSection: §4 (design rule: no code exposes a raw AudioParam or setter to the UI)
findings.description: The param package's public barrel re-exports `writeAudioParam` and `ParamHandleImpl` (line 51), and that barrel is what the UI imports — `src/app/App.tsx` does `import { fromNormalized, toNormalized } from "../params"`. `writeAudioParam(param, value, when, smoothingMs)` is literally the raw-AudioParam setter the §4 design rule names, sitting in the UI's import surface; only the fact that no UI-reachable object hands out an `AudioParam` keeps the rule intact today. It is consumed solely by `src/devices/harness/deviceInstance.ts`, which already deep-imports `../../params/handle`, so it does not need to be on the barrel at all.

findings.planSection: §4 (`onChange(cb)` — UI repaint, coalesced to rAF) / §5
findings.description: The one live control never subscribes through the sanctioned read half of the bridge: `handleBoot` seeds `cutoffNorm`/`cutoffText` once from `cutoff.live()` and thereafter the readout is driven only by the component's own `setCutoffNorm`/`setCutoffText` inside `handleCutoffInput`. `handle.onChange(...)` is never called, so any write that does not originate in this input — an automation-path `setLive(v,'automation')` in M3, a registry `load()`, a `setBase` from undo — leaves the slider and its `toText` readout stale, and the `base()` ghost-dot/override states §4 defines have no subscription to render from. The registry's rAF coalescing (`src/params/frame.ts`) exists for exactly this and is currently exercised only by tests.

The M0 audible proof clips. Rendering DEMO_CLIP through core.poly-synth -> core.filter -> destination on a real OfflineAudioContext (via window.__fabletonDemo.renderDemoOffline) gives peakAbs = 1.451 and 6172 of 220500 samples (2.80%) with |sample| > 1.0, i.e. up to +3.2 dBFS. I measured the same on the live graph through an AnalyserNode tap (peak 1.08 in a 2048-sample window). Cause: DEMO_CLIP hard-codes vel = 100 (0.787 linear) with NOTE_DUR = 440 ticks against a 480-tick spacing and a 250 ms release, so two voices overlap on every note boundary while core.poly-synth's `gain` defaults to 0 dB and neither the device nor the demo chain leaves headroom (src/devices/core/polySynth.ts `p.db("gain", ..., { default: 0 })`, src/demo/engine.ts connects filter.output straight to the destination). On real hardware the destination hard-clips, so the milestone's one audible deliverable is distorted on every playback. §18-M0 only requires the clip be audible, so this is polish, not an acceptance failure.

findings.planSection: §4 (Value semantics / toText) + §14 (p.* helper library)
findings.description: One dB descriptor carries two contradictory meanings for its minimum, so the readout lies for the shipped instrument. `p.db("gain", "Gain", { min: -60, max: 6, default: 0 })` sets silenceBelow = -60 (descriptors.ts), so `desc.toText(-60)` returns "-inf dB" (src/params/text.ts formatDb), and `gainForValue(desc, -60)` in src/devices/harness/deviceInstance.ts returns exactly 0 for the gain-node fast path. But core.poly-synth's `gain` is bound with `bindAudioParam` and the worklet computes `10 ** (gain / 20)` (src/worklets/poly-synth-processor.ts), i.e. 0.001 — still audible. Verified by probe: toText(-60) = "-inf dB" | gainForValue(-60) = 0 | worklet linear = 0.001. §4 makes `toText` the sanctioned readout of the real-unit value, so a param whose readout says silence while the DSP is at -60 dBFS (and whose meaning flips depending on which fast path a device happens to pick) is a divergence in the descriptor library M4's six devices will copy.

findings.planSection: §12 (Guardrails: "zero allocation in per-tick paths (preallocated event objects, ring buffers for messages)")
findings.description: The scheduler -> instrument message path allocates one object literal per note event, per tick. `post({ type: "noteOn", pitch, vel, when })` / `post({ type: "noteOff", pitch, when })` in PolySynth.create build a fresh payload for every event the transport schedules inside each 25 ms look-ahead window. The rest of the codebase honours the guardrail explicitly and shows the fix is available: src/workers/clock.worker.ts reuses one `tickMessage` object across postMessage (structured clone makes reuse safe), src/engine/transport/clipEventSource.ts reuses one NoteEvent plus its iterator result, and transport.ts keeps all bookkeeping in preallocated typed arrays — all three carry comments citing this very guardrail. Main-thread only, so the cost is GC jitter in the UI thread rather than an audio dropout, hence minor; but it is the one per-tick path in M0 that does not meet the stated §12 rule.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Guardrails: "zero allocation in per-tick paths (preallocated event objects, ring buffers for messages)")
findings.description: The per-tick scheduling path allocates one object per note event, at both ends of the postMessage hop. `polySynth.ts:81-89` builds a fresh literal for every event the scheduler emits: `noteOn` -> `post({ type:"noteOn", pitch, vel, when })`, `noteOff` -> `post({ type:"noteOff", pitch, when })`, `allNotesOff` -> `post({ type:"allNotesOff", when })`. These are called directly from `transport.scheduleWindow` (transport.ts:331/335) on every worker tick, and from `panic()` on every stop/seek/tempo change (which emits one object per still-pending note plus one per track). Every other link in that chain was deliberately built allocation-free and says so in its header — `clipEventSource.ts:275-320` preallocates the event, the iterator, and both IteratorResult objects; `transport.ts:17-21` uses only typed arrays and index loops; `clock.worker.ts:206-209` reuses a single `tickMessage` because "the tick path runs 40x/second forever". The guardrail is broken only at the final hop, and it is broken in the one place the plan calls out by name: the main-thread literal is trivially avoidable (postMessage structured-clones synchronously, so three preallocated payload objects can be reused exactly as clock.worker.ts already does), and the second half — `poly-synth-processor.ts:87-89`, where `port.onmessage` receives a freshly deserialized object per event inside the AudioWorkletGlobalScope — is allocation and GC pressure *on the audio render thread*, which is precisely what "ring buffers for messages" in the guardrail exists to prevent (a GC pause there is a dropout, not just jank). At M0's one-note-at-a-time demo this is invisible; at SS2's stated budget (16 tracks, 40 concurrent voices) it is hundreds of objects per second churning on both threads. Nothing in the codebase currently satisfies the guardrail's message clause.

findings.planSection: SS7 (device swap/removal is gain-ramped; "click-free") / SS12 (audio-thread guardrails)
findings.description: Un-ramped amplitude step when a voice is stolen or retriggered at a different velocity. `applyDue` (line 157-158) writes `voice.velocity = vel` instantly, and the render loop computes `mix += oscillatorSample(...) * amplitude * voice.velocity` (line 134). `AdsrEnvelope.noteOn` deliberately does NOT reset the level — envelope.ts:198-200 states the reason: "a retriggered/stolen voice ramps from wherever it currently is, avoiding a hard discontinuity when the voice allocator reuses a still-sounding voice", and VoiceAllocator's LRU policy (voiceAllocator.ts:48-56) is justified by the same goal. The instantaneous velocity write defeats that for exactly the case it was designed for: steal a voice sitting at envelope level 0.8 with velocity 1.0 for a new note at velocity 0.2 and the sample value jumps from 0.8 to 0.16 in one sample — a click, on the audio thread, in the code path the surrounding comments claim is click-free. Reachable whenever a 9th simultaneous note arrives (MAX_VOICES = 8) or the same pitch is retriggered at a different velocity while its release tail is still running. Masked in M0 only because DEMO_CLIP is monophonic at a constant velocity of 100 (demo/clip.ts:21).

findings.planSection: SS2 (Performance budgets: glitch-free at ~16 tracks / ~40 concurrent voices at the 128-sample quantum)
findings.description: Loop-invariant transcendentals recomputed per sample inside the render quantum. `OnePoleLowpass.process` (lines 61-67) recomputes `alpha = 1 - Math.exp(-2*PI*clamped/sampleRate)` on every sample, although `cutoffHz` is read once per block from a k-rate AudioParam (poly-synth-processor.ts:102) and cannot change within the block; and the voice loop calls `midiToFrequencyHz(voice.pitch ?? 0)` (line 132) per sample per voice, although the pitch is fixed for the life of the note and the phase increment could be computed once at note-on. The filter's exp also runs on every sample of every block forever, even when all voices are idle, because `process()` always returns true and always runs the full sample loop. I benchmarked the exact arithmetic of that inner loop (8 voices, sine shape, 48 kHz, 10 s of audio, node/V8): as written 343 ms vs 215 ms with the exp hoisted to per-block and the phase increment to per-note — 1.6x, i.e. ~17% of one core versus ~11% at SS2's ~40-voice budget, purely for values that are constant. Not a glitch source at M0's scale, but it is avoidable work on the render thread and it scales with the exact figure SS2 fixes a budget for.

findings.planSection: SS12 (worker clock protocol; `ClockTickMessage.seq` for drop detection)
findings.description: The worker-clock protocol has no epoch, so ticks already in flight when the transport stops are mis-attributed to the next run. `createWorkerClock.start()` (lines 100-103) calls `sink.reset()` — which sets `expectedSeq = 0` — and posts `{type:"start"}`; the worker independently resets `seq = 0` (clock.worker.ts:220). But `stop()` only posts a message: ticks the worker already posted before it processed the stop are sitting in the main thread's task queue and are delivered *after* the reset. `createTickSink.emit` (lines 49-55) then sees `seq = N` against `expectedSeq = 0` and does `dropped += N`. After a 10-second play/stop/play cycle, `EngineTransport.droppedTicks` — the transport's only scheduler-health diagnostic (transport.ts:76-79) — jumps by several hundred phantom drops, and the next real drop is then hidden because `expectedSeq` was pushed to N+1. Scheduling itself is unaffected (it is time-based and the stale ticks are harmless no-ops), but the one signal that would tell you the 25 ms clock is being starved is unreliable exactly after the operation a user performs most. `createTimerClock` is not affected — it clears its interval synchronously. A generation/epoch id echoed back in `ClockTickMessage` would make stale ticks identifiable.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling — loop-brace unrolling; stuck notes)
findings.description: The loop-brace note-cut bookkeeping de-duplicates by (pitch, track), so overlapping same-pitch notes leave a held note untracked and uncut at the brace. `markSounding` (lines 232-243) returns early if the pitch/track pair is already present, and `clearSounding` (lines 245-254) removes the single entry on the first note-off. For two overlapping notes of the same pitch — note A [0,1000), note B [500,1500), brace at 1200 — the sequence is markSounding(60) at 0, no-op at 500, clearSounding(60) at 1000; at the brace `cutSounding` (line 257) believes nothing is held, so B never receives the note-off that the half-open window (`eventsInRange` is exclusive of the brace, and playback jumps back to `loop.start`) will never emit either. That is precisely the sustaining-forever case the block comment at lines 218-223 says this machinery exists to prevent. It is masked in M0 by the instrument, not by the transport: `VoiceAllocator.allocate` (voiceAllocator.ts:57-68) is one-voice-per-pitch, so the earlier note-off already released the shared voice. Any instrument that voices overlapping same-pitch notes separately — and any M1 piano roll that lets a user draw them — gets a stuck note across the brace.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling) — loop-brace unrolling / "Stop sends allNotesOff" note-lifetime invariant
findings.description: The loop-brace note cut leaks a stuck note when two same-pitch notes on one track overlap. The sounding-note ledger (markSounding, lines 232-243; clearSounding, 245-254; cutSounding, 256-268) is keyed only by (pitch, trackId) AND deduped: markSounding returns early if (pitch,track) is already present, and clearSounding removes the single entry on the first note-off it sees. So when note A (p60, ticks 0..1200) and note B (p60, ticks 900..2900) overlap, scheduleWindow (line 333) marks p60 once at A's onset, B's noteOn at 900 is a no-op for the ledger, and A's noteOff at 1200 (line 336) clears the entry — leaving B untracked. When the cursor reaches the brace, cutSounding finds nothing to release and B never receives a note-off, which is precisely the failure the block comment at lines 218-223 says this bookkeeping exists to prevent ("a note held across the transport loop brace would never receive its note-off and would sustain forever"). Substantiated repro (scratchpad/t7.ts): clip {length 3840, notes a=[0,1200) p60, b=[900,2900) p60}, transport loop {start:0,end:1920,enabled:true}, 120 bpm, manual clock at 20 ms, fake ctx. Emitted stream per pass is `on 60 @0.0050 | on 60 @0.4738 | off 60 @0.6300` and then straight to the next pass's `on 60 @1.0050` — the expected `off 60 @1.0050` from cutSounding is absent, every pass, forever. Nothing in MidiClip (src/types/clip.ts) forbids overlapping same-pitch notes and clipEventSource emits their on/off pairs correctly, so the loss is purely in the transport's ledger. Fix direction: key the ledger per scheduled note occurrence (or refcount per pitch) instead of deduping by pitch.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling) — guardrail "resume the context on first user gesture (Safari)"
findings.description: The unlock listener is strictly one-shot and cannot re-enter, so a resume that does not stick leaves the app permanently silent. handleGesture (lines 51-60) sets `unlocked = true` and calls detach() BEFORE `context.resume()`, and the rejection path is `.catch(() => {})` — there is no re-arm. If the first gesture's resume rejects or resolves with the context still "suspended" (the exact Safari behaviour the module header describes), no subsequent gesture will ever retry; recovery requires a page reload. Compounding it, the `context.state === "running"` early-out (line 39) is sampled once at attach time, so a context that the UA later suspends (iOS interruption, backgrounded tab) has nothing armed at all — and bootAudioContext (src/engine/context/boot.ts:44-45) awaits resume() first, so on the happy path no listener is ever attached. A correct one-shot re-checks `context.state` after the resume settles and only then detaches.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling) — two-clock design (look-ahead must exceed the tick period)
findings.description: `lookAheadSeconds` is validated only as `> 0` (lines 105-108), but the scheduler silently degrades — playing slower than real time — once the look-ahead is at or below START_LEAD_SECONDS (0.005 s, line 50) or the tick period. Each tick, restartCursor/re-anchor puts cursorTime at `now + 0.005` while the horizon is `now + lookAhead`; when lookAhead <= 0.005 the `while (cursorTime < horizon)` loop (line 374) schedules little or nothing, then the next tick sees `cursorTime < now` and takes the re-anchor branch (lines 366-370), discarding the elapsed time. Measured (scratchpad/t8.ts, 120 bpm, 5 ms clock steps, 2 s of audio time, expected ~3830 ticks): lookAhead 0.2 s -> positionTicks 3830; 0.01 s -> 3830; 0.005 s -> 2527; 0.004 s -> 1600; 0.001 s -> 400 with only 1 of 4 note-ons ever scheduled. Nothing in TransportDeps (src/types/transport.ts:109) documents the floor, and the failure is silent rather than an error.

findings.planSection: SS7 (Device system) — voice allocator behind noteOn/noteOff/allNotesOff
findings.description: `clear()` (lines 56-62) resets `order[i] = -1` and `nextOrder = 0`, throwing away exactly the last-used stamps that the class's own doc comment (lines 26-31) says are the reason allocation is least-recently-used rather than lowest-index ("Handing out slot 0 every time would ... truncate every release tail"). Because `allNotesOff` in PolySynthProcessor.applyDue calls `allocator.clear()` while the just-released voices are still ringing out their envelope release, the pool reverts to lowest-index allocation after every transport panic — which is every stop(), seek(), and setTempoMap() while playing (transport.ts panic(), lines 408-428). Demonstrated (scratchpad/ta.ts): a four-note monophonic melody with release between notes picks voices 0,1,2,3 normally, but 0,0,0,0 when a clear() lands between notes, so each new note truncates the previous note's still-sounding release tail.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling) — "Stop sends allNotesOff(now + e) down every track"
findings.description: The allNotesOff branch of applyDue (lines 168-176) skips every voice whose allocator slot is already null (`if (this.allocator.pitchOf(v) === null) continue`), so voices that were released earlier and are still ringing out their release tail are untouched by a panic — allNotesOff only converts held voices to release, it never silences. That may be a deliberate choice, but AdsrEnvelope.reset() (src/devices/core/polySynth/envelope.ts:81-85) is documented verbatim as "Forces the voice fully off, immediately (used by allNotesOff panics)" and is dead code: grep finds no caller anywhere in src/ outside its own unit test. Either the panic should use reset() as its own doc claims, or that doc comment is wrong about who calls it — as it stands the two disagree about what stop() guarantees.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling) — the event iterator's note-on/note-off pairing
findings.description: After a loop-brace wrap (or a play(fromTick)/seek into the middle of a note), the source emits unpaired note-offs. beginWindow -> seekWithinSegment (lines 167-174) positions offIdx with `lowerBound(p.offKeys, contentPos)`, and the skip loop in step() (lines 190-194) only rejects notes whose start falls outside the current REPETITION, not outside the current window. So a note starting before the window's fromTick but ending inside it yields a noteOff with no preceding noteOn on that pass. Measured over 300 randomized brace runs (scratchpad/t5.ts): 1581 orphan note-offs reaching the NoteTarget, 0 double-ons, 0 stuck notes. It is benign for core.poly-synth only because VoiceAllocator.release() returns null for an unheld pitch; the NoteTarget contract (src/types/transport.ts:81-85) makes no such promise, so any future instrument that trusts on/off pairing (or any track where two same-pitch notes overlap, see the major finding) will cut a live voice early.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) / SS3-SS4 (param write paths)
findings.description: The only place the shipped app writes to the engine — the filter-cutoff control implementing SS3 fast path A (`handleCutoffInput` -> `handle.setLive(real, "user")`, `handleCutoffCommit` -> `handle.commit()`), plus the post-boot seeding of `cutoffNorm`/`cutoffText` and the synchronous `bootingRef` double-boot guard (whose own comment describes a real failure: a second AudioContext + chain leaking) — has zero coverage at any level. `src/app/App.test.tsx` is 27 lines of `renderToStaticMarkup` (string matching on the pre-boot markup only); no e2e spec references the control (`grep -rn 'filter-cutoff\|setLive\|commit' e2e/` -> no hits; the e2e suite only clicks Boot/Play/Stop). Substantiated by mutation on a scratch copy of the repo: replacing `handle.setLive(real, "user")` with `void real;` and `cutoffRef.current?.commit()` with `void cutoffRef.current;` — i.e. the slider moves and the readout updates but the DSP never hears the gesture and nothing is ever committed — still gives `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx vitest run` 315/315 passed, and `npx playwright test` 11/11 passed. Nothing headless (jsdom + react-dom/client is enough) or in e2e pins this seam, so an M0-acceptance claim that the shipped app exercises the SS4 bridge rests on no test.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — "tempo map ... no browser needed"; SS8 (integer ticks)
findings.description: `TempoMap.ticksAt` is the seconds->ticks half of SS8's conversion boundary and its nearest-rounding is explicitly load-bearing for the scheduler (src/engine/transport/transport.ts: "`>=`, not `>`: `ticksAt` rounds, so a window boundary landing exactly on `loop.end` is an ordinary outcome"), yet no test pins the rounding direction. The two relevant tests only assert `Number.isInteger(...)` and round-trips at exactly representable ticks. Mutation on a scratch copy: changing `return Math.round(raw);` (src/time/tempoMap.ts:115) to `Math.floor(raw)` leaves the entire suite green (315/315 across all of src), even though it is a real ±1-tick behavior change (at 120 bpm / 960 PPQ, `ticksAt(0.1234)` is 237 rounded vs 236 floored) that would shift the playhead, look-ahead window ends and loop-brace detection. (`Math.ceil` is killed, so only the downward-biased half of the contract is unguarded.) A single assertion on a non-exact input would close it.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — "no browser needed for any of the load-bearing logic"; SS12 (two-clock design)
findings.description: `createWorkerClock` — the clock that actually drives the look-ahead scheduler in the shipped app (`createDefaultClock` returns it whenever `Worker` exists) — has no headless test at all. jsdom has no `Worker`, so `clock.test.ts` only covers `createTimerClock`, the `createDefaultClock` no-Worker fallback, and the worker-side protocol (`src/workers/clock.worker.ts`, driven through `window`). The main-thread half's untested logic: `ClockTickMessage` validation, `post()` suppression after `dispose()`, `worker.terminate()`, and the shared `createTickSink` drop accounting. Substantiated by mutation on a scratch copy: deleting the tick-message guard `if (message.type !== "tick" || typeof message.seq !== "number") return;` and, separately, deleting the drop accounting `if (seq > expectedSeq) dropped += seq - expectedSeq;` both leave the suite green — the latter because the only `droppedTicks` assertion (transport.test.ts:286) runs through `createManualClock`, which reimplements the same drop arithmetic in src/engine/transport/manualClock.ts (itself untested as a unit). The class is trivially testable without a browser by stubbing `globalThis.Worker`; today the only proof is a browser e2e (e2e/interaction/transport.spec.ts), which is exactly what SS15 says should not be necessary.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — scheduler unit tests; SS7 (device swap), SS12 (stop is silent)
findings.description: Several documented, deliberately-written scheduler behaviors survive mutation, i.e. are unasserted: (1) the per-tick reset of the target cache (`cachedTrack = null; cachedTarget = undefined;` in `onTick`, whose comment cites SS7 instrument swap between ticks) — deleting it changes nothing because every test's `resolveTarget` returns a constant target; (2) the `stop()` overflow fallback `if (pendingOverflowed) target?.allNotesOff(at + lookAhead);` and the `cutSounding` overflow fallback that broadcasts `allNotesOff` when the sounding ring overflows — no test ever fills the 1024/512-entry rings, so both SS12 "stop is silent" safety nets are dead code as far as the suite knows; (3) the anchor ring wrap (`ANCHOR_CAPACITY` 256 -> 2 changes nothing); (4) the position clamps in `positionTicks`/`positionSeconds` (`if (tick > end) return end`, the `endSeconds` clamp) — `positionSeconds` is asserted in only two places (stopped-at-0 and one linear playback reading) and never across a loop brace. Each deletion was applied on a scratch copy and the transport suite stayed green.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — scheduler unit tests; SS8 (TempoMap)
findings.description: The scheduler is never tested against a multi-segment `TempoMap`: transport.test.ts imports only `createFixedTempoMap`, and the one tempo test swaps one fixed map for another (`setTempoMap(createFixedTempoMap(240))`). `scheduleWindow` computes every event's audio time as a `tempoMap.secondsAt` difference across the window, so a tempo boundary falling *inside* a look-ahead window (the piecewise-integration path that tempoMap.test.ts covers in isolation) is untested at the seam SS8 says the conversion lives at. Cheap to add with the existing `makeRig` + `createTempoMap([...])`.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — "schedule a clip, render, assert on the buffer"
findings.description: The buffer assertions of the SS15 integration proof rest entirely on `analyze()` (peak/RMS/per-window RMS), which is pure, headless-testable arithmetic with no unit test and no export to make one possible — only `renderDemoOffline` and `RMS_WINDOW_SECONDS` leave the module. If `windowRms` bucketing or the RMS accumulation were wrong, e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts's "energy in the first third and middle third, decayed in the last window" assertions would pass vacuously, and nothing else in the repo would notice. Exporting `analyze` and feeding it a synthetic AudioBuffer-shaped stub would pin the measurement the milestone's audibility claim depends on.
