rejected.finding: Finding 1 (major), second half: the freshly deserialized object `port.onmessage` receives per event inside the AudioWorkletGlobalScope is allocation on the render thread and should be replaced per §12's "ring buffers for messages".
rejected.reason: Partially deferred, not dropped. The main-thread half is fixed (preallocated payloads). The receive-side object is created by the platform's structured clone; the only way to remove it is a SharedArrayBuffer ring shared with the audio thread, which is a design piece §6's metering work owns (the COOP/COEP headers it needs are already in vite.config.ts). Doing it inside this round would mean inventing the ring protocol M0 has no other user for. The processor already copies each event straight into its preallocated typed-array queue and retains nothing, so the deserialized object is short-lived and nothing else per-event allocates on that thread; the constraint and the plan are documented at the call site in polySynth.ts.

rejected.finding: Finding 20 (minor), item (3): "the anchor ring wrap (ANCHOR_CAPACITY 256 -> 2 changes nothing)".
rejected.reason: Not a defect and not worth pinning. The overflow branch in `pushAnchor` is unreachable by construction: `anchorFor` retires finished passes on every tick and at most MAX_PASSES_PER_TICK (64) passes are pushed between two retirements, so the count cannot reach 256. ANCHOR_CAPACITY is a tuning constant — any value >= 2 preserves every observable invariant (a smaller ring just keeps less history, which `positionTicks()` clamps for), which is exactly why the mutation is silent. I verified this empirically: with capacity 2, and separately with the `anchorCount--` drop removed, the new short-brace test (>256 passes, position asserted inside the brace at every tick) still passes. I kept the guard as defensive code and documented why it cannot fire today rather than writing a test that asserts a constant.

findings.planSection: SS8 (Musical time model — "always integer" ticks) / SS12
findings.description: `play()` and `seek()` defensively `Math.round(tick)`, but the loop brace does not: `createEngineTransport`'s `deps.loop` and `Transport.setLoop()` store the region verbatim (`loop = {...next}`), and `onTick` then feeds `loop.end` / `loop.start` straight into `scheduleWindow`, `closeLastAnchor` and `pushAnchor` -> `tempoMap.secondsAt(tick)`. Reproduced with a probe: constructing the transport with `loop: { start: 0, end: 960.5, enabled: true }` and ticking a manual clock throws `TempoMap.secondsAt(tick): expected an integer tick value, got 960.5` from inside the scheduler tick — playback dies with no recovery path (the throw escapes `onTick`, which is the clock subscriber). In a production build the dev-only `assertIntegerTicks` guard is compiled out, so the same input instead silently propagates fractional ticks into `cursorTick`/`windowEnd` and the anchor ring, breaking SS8's "ALWAYS an integer" invariant rather than failing loudly. No M0 UI sets a loop, so acceptance is unaffected; M1's loop brace will hit this boundary. Rounding (or validating) in `setLoop`/the deps read, the way `play`/`seek` already do, closes it.

findings.planSection: SS12 (Transport & scheduling — "Stop sends allNotesOff(now + ε) down every track")
findings.description: `panic()` sends `allNotesOff` only to `seenTracks` — the set of track ids that had at least one event scheduled with a resolvable target since the current playback pass began (`seenTracks` is cleared in `beginPlayback` and `seek`). SS12's wording is "down every track". In M0 this is behaviourally equivalent (one track, and every note reaching an instrument goes through `scheduleWindow`, which is what populates `seenTracks`), so nothing sticks today; it becomes a real narrowing as soon as a channel's instrument can receive notes from a path other than the current scheduling pass — SS12's own metronome/count-in click instrument on a hidden channel, or MIDI-input capture in the `recording` state. Worth widening to "every channel the resolver can produce" when that lands rather than leaving the divergence latent.

findings.planSection: SS15 (Stack — "worklets as separate entry points; solve once in M0")
findings.description: The header comment on the file that exists specifically to document SS15's worklet-bundling seam states the module "is loaded via `audioContext.audioWorklet.addModule(...)` using the `?url` import suffix (see src/engine/context)". The actual seam in `src/engine/context/audioContext.ts` uses `?worker&url`, and its own comment records that plain `?url` was tried and rejected because it copies untranspiled TS for a `.ts` source. Two files now give contradicting accounts of the one nonstandard build decision M0 is supposed to settle; the stale one is the file a future device author is most likely to copy.

findings.planSection: SS12
findings.description: The stall-recovery re-anchor in `onTick` (lines 378-389) moves the timeline but never releases the notes it has already handed the instrument, so any note sounding when the main thread stalls drones for the whole stall. `cursorTime` jumps to `now + START_LEAD`, `cursorTick` is unchanged, so every event after the stall — including the pending note-OFF of a note whose note-ON was already delivered — is emitted shifted by the stall duration. Verified end-to-end with a headless rig (transport -> real NoteEventQueue -> real PolySynthProcessor, 48 kHz, DEMO_CLIP): with the tick loop suppressed for 2 s from t=0.6 s while ctx.currentTime keeps running, the scheduler emits `noteOn(72)@0.755` then `noteOff(72)@2.813` for a note written 440 ticks (229 ms) long — the voice sustains for 2.06 s, and the rendered output is a flat ~0.19 RMS drone for ~2 s (a 300 ms stall stretches it by ~105 ms; the stretch is unbounded in the stall length). This is exactly what SS12's 'jitter in the tick loop never reaches the audio' promises will not happen, and the stall path is the one the 25 ms worker clock exists to survive. The transport already owns the fix pattern for an identical timeline discontinuity: `cutSounding(when)` is called at the loop brace (transport.ts:412-415) precisely so a note spanning the jump is released rather than left sustaining; the re-anchor branch calls `closeLastAnchor` but not `cutSounding`. The existing test 'transport — main-thread stalls' (transport.test.ts:469) only asserts no timestamp lands in the past and uses 100-tick notes, so nothing covers a note held across the re-anchor.

findings.planSection: SS7
findings.description: `allocate()` (lines 32-43) retriggers the existing voice when the pitch is already sounding, and `release()` (lines 46-53) frees that single slot — so two overlapping same-pitch notes on one track share one voice and the FIRST note-off releases both. Concretely: notes (pitch 60, ticks 0..1920) and (pitch 60, ticks 960..1440) produce on60, on60, off60@1440, off60@1920; the second off finds nothing and the sound stops at tick 1440 instead of 1920. The transport goes out of its way to support this exact case — its sounding-note ledger is deliberately not deduplicated by (pitch, track) with the comment 'two notes of the same pitch on one track may overlap ... M1's piano roll lets a user draw it' (transport.ts:246-251) — and the instrument silently undoes that guarantee on the audio thread. Harmless for M0's DEMO_CLIP (no overlaps), real as soon as the piano roll lands.

findings.planSection: SS12
findings.description: SS12's guardrail is 'zero allocation in per-tick paths (preallocated event objects, ring buffers for messages)'. The main-thread half is done (one reused payload per message type, lines 84-115), but every scheduled note still crosses the thread boundary as a structured-cloned `port.postMessage`, so the AUDIO RENDER thread allocates and GCs one fresh object per note event inside `port.onmessage` (poly-synth-processor.ts:116-118) — the half of the guardrail that actually protects against a dropout. The 'ring buffers for messages' clause is not implemented, and the COOP/COEP headers a SharedArrayBuffer ring would need are already in place (vite.config.ts). The code documents the deferral honestly (polySynth.ts:64-83), so this is a knowing partial implementation rather than an oversight, and the event rate in M0 is low — but the guardrail is not met as written.

findings.planSection: SS7
findings.description: `rampOutAndDisconnect` (lines 272-290) and `writeAudioParam` (params/handle.ts:256-272) anchor a ramp that starts in the FUTURE at the param's value read NOW: `const from = param.value; cancelScheduledValues(at); setValueAtTime(from, at); linearRampToValueAtTime(0, at + rampMs)`. When `dispose(when)` is called with a future `when` — which the API explicitly supports (`DeviceInstance.dispose(when?)`, `AppDeviceHost.unmount(id, when)`) and which SS7's swap flow ('~20 ms crossfade', 'old disposed after its tail') will use — anything that moves that gain between now and `when` is overwritten by a step back to the stale `from` value at `when`, i.e. a click at the start of the fade-out that the fade exists to prevent. Latent in M0 (the only gains passed here are the devices' own unautomated output gains, so `from` is always 1.0), but it is the same primitive M2's reconciler patches are meant to ramp with.

findings.planSection: SS12
findings.description:
Clip-loop unrolling emits spurious, unpaired note-offs whenever a look-ahead window boundary happens to land exactly on a clip-loop repetition boundary after a jump (transport brace wrap, seek, or play(fromTick)). In beginWindow (line 280) the boundary back-up `enterSegment(p, k - 1)` runs through enterSegment, which unconditionally does `if (k !== p.seg) p.orphanCutoff = -Infinity;` (line 157). seekWithinSegment then only re-arms the cutoff when `jumped` is true (line 282 -> line 186), and `jumped` is false for a window that continues the previous one. The orphan suppression established by the jump is therefore silently discarded, and step() (line 214) re-emits the note-offs of notes whose note-ons were never emitted on this pass.

Minimal repro (clip length 2000, loop {start:100,end:800}, notes: {start 0, dur 5000, pitch 61} and {start 600, dur 100, pitch 60}); the only difference is where the window is split:
  eventsInRange(500,1000)                     -> 600 noteOn 60, 700 noteOff 60
  eventsInRange(500,800); eventsInRange(800,1000) -> 600 noteOn 60, 700 noteOff 60, 800 noteOff 61   <-- extra, unpaired
  eventsInRange(500,700); eventsInRange(700,1000) -> 600 noteOn 60, 700 noteOff 60
A randomized differential over 1499 clips (one jump then a random contiguous partition vs. the same range as one window) produced 15 EXTRA events and 0 MISSING; every extra one sat on a repetition boundary.

This is not benign at the transport level. Driven through createEngineTransport with a ManualClock (120 bpm, lookAhead 0.2 s, 5 ms steps, brace {start:400,end:2000}, clip A = loop {100,800} with a long pitch-61 intro note, clip B = a live pitch-61 note at tick 500 on the same track), the resurrected `noteOff(61)` at tick 800 (a) releases clip B's genuinely live voice ~0.6 s early - it lasted 0.156 s instead of the 0.78 s it lasted on cycles where the boundary fell elsewhere - and (b) is fed to transport.clearSounding(), which removes clip B's entry from the `sounding` ledger, so cutSounding() at the brace end releases nothing. Because the window boundary is determined by the wall clock, the wrong audio appears intermittently. clipEventSource.ts's own header states the NoteTarget contract promises on/off pairing, and SS12 requires the iterator to unroll clip loops and the brace correctly.

Coverage gap: the guard test at clipEventSource.test.ts:329 ('emits no orphan note-offs across a transport loop brace') uses a clip with no `loop` field, so the repetition-boundary reset is never exercised; the partition test at line 279 never jumps.

findings.planSection: SS12
findings.description: onTick()'s multi-pass scheduling loop (line 393) checks `state === "stopped"` only on entry (line 369) and never re-checks, even though it calls out to caller-supplied code inside the loop - `fillers[i].fillWindow(endTime, fromTick, toTick)` at line 362 and `resolveTarget` via targetFor. A WindowFiller that calls transport.stop() therefore sees state flip to 'stopped' and the panic allNotesOff go out, and then the loop keeps scheduling: with a brace {start:0,end:PPQ*2} and lookAheadSeconds 3, stopping inside the first fillWindow still delivered 8 further noteOn calls at 1.005 s ... 2.755 s. Those note-ons are posted AFTER the panic message, so NoteEventQueue.cancelFrom (which purges at push time) cannot drop them, and the instrument would keep sounding for up to a full look-ahead while transport.state reads 'stopped'. beginPlayback guards exactly this class of re-entrancy (`if (stateIsStopped(state)) return;` after setState); onTick does not. Not reachable from M0's own wiring - the demo registers no filler and its resolveTarget is a pure lookup - but addWindowFiller is shipped M0 API and SS11's automation sampler is its documented consumer.

findings.planSection: SS12
findings.description: The unlock listeners detach permanently after the first successful resume, contradicting the module's own documented contract. The header states: 'they stay armed for a context that is already running too, so a context the UA suspends later (iOS interruption, backgrounded tab) is unlocked again by the next gesture.' The code does `if (context.state === "running") detach();` (line 79) inside the post-resume continuation, so once our resume sticks the listener set is gone. Verified with a fake gesture target and a fake context: first pointerdown -> resume called, state 'running', 0 listeners remaining; then the UA suspends the context; a second pointerdown does nothing and the context stays 'suspended' forever, recoverable only by a page reload - precisely the failure mode the header says the design avoids. Only the branch where the context was ALREADY running when the gesture arrived (early return at line 68) keeps the listeners armed. SS12's stated guardrail ('resume the context on first user gesture (Safari)') is still met for the first unlock, so this is a robustness/doc-vs-code gap rather than a milestone failure. Related nit in the same area: bootAudioContext (src/engine/context/boot.ts:46) discards the Unsub returned by unlockAudioContextOnGesture, so a second boot leaks a second listener set.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — "the engine runs headless against OfflineAudioContext … schedule a clip, render, assert on the buffer"; SS18-M0 "a hard-coded clip audible through a hard-coded chain"
SS15 (testing) — "assert on the buffer"; SS4 fast path A
findings.description: The only real-audio assertions in the project are level-only: peakAbs > 0.01, rms > 0.001, peakAbs < 1, clippedSamples === 0, and a coarse per-50 ms RMS envelope. Nothing spectral, nothing per-onset, and no A/B render. Consequences: (1) the render cannot observe whether core.filter processed the signal at all (see the major finding); (2) SS4 fast path A is never proven against rendered samples anywhere — e2e/interaction/param-control.spec.ts asserts handle.live()/base() and the readout string, and src/params/handle.test.ts asserts recorded FakeAudioParam events, so a cutoff write that reaches a BiquadFilterNode that is not in the path (or is bound to the wrong AudioParam at the assembly level) is invisible; (3) a render that dropped half the notes or played wrong pitches still satisfies every assertion. The cheap fix the seam already supports: render twice via renderDemoOffline with different cutoff values and assert the level/high-frequency content differs — no new production code needed.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — load-bearing scheduler logic must be unit-tested without a browser
findings.description: `prunePending(now)` (called at the top of `onTick`) has no test. Deleting the call leaves all 359 unit tests passing (verified by mutation). It is not dead code: `panic()` skips already-elapsed entries by time, so pruning is what keeps the PENDING ring bounded — without it `pendingCount` grows once per note-on for the whole of a continuous playback, hits PENDING_CAPACITY (1024), sets `pendingOverflowed`, and silently degrades every subsequent `stop()` into the broadcast `allNotesOff(at)` + `allNotesOff(at + lookAhead)` fallback that the per-note ledger exists to avoid. transport.test.ts covers the overflow *fallback* (line 763) but never the pruning that is supposed to prevent reaching it, and this is trivially testable headlessly with the ManualClock harness already in that file.

findings.planSection: SS8 (musical time model, "always integer" ticks) + SS15 (scheduler unit-tested without a browser)
findings.description: The integer-tick normalization at the transport's two public entry points is untested. Replacing `Math.round(fromTick)` in `play()` with `fromTick`, and separately `const target = Math.round(tick)` in `seek()` with `const target = tick`, both leave all 359 unit tests passing (verified by mutation). A fractional tick from either entry point flows into `tempoMap.secondsAt(...)` and `positionTicks()`; in a dev build it throws from the integrality guard, and in a production build (where src/time/dev.ts's `isDev` is false) it silently propagates. transport.test.ts has "play(fromTick) starts there…" and "seek moves the playhead…" but every case passes an integer.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing) — tempo map unit-tested; SS8 TempoMap invariants
findings.description: Six of the tempo-map tests pin behavior that does not exist in the shipped build. `validateSegments` enforces positive-finite bpm and integer startTick through `assertPositiveFinite` / `assertIntegerTicks` in /workspaces/fableton/src/time/dev.ts, which no-op when `import.meta.env.DEV` is false; Vite statically replaces that with `false` in a production build. So "throws on non-integer startTick", "throws on non-positive bpm", and the two "dev-mode integrality guard" cases pass under Vitest (dev) while `createTempoMap([{startTick:0,bpm:0}])` in the shipped bundle returns a map producing Infinity/NaN seconds — despite the doc comment on `createTempoMap` promising "Throws if the segment invariants (SS8) are violated". No test runs any of src/time/ in the production configuration (e.g. with NODE_ENV=production or a stubbed `import.meta.env.DEV`), so nothing pins which validations actually ship.

fixed: MAJOR (SS12) src/engine/transport/transport.ts — stall re-anchor left held notes droning. onTick's re-anchor branch now calls cutSounding(cursorTime) after moving cursorTime to now + START_LEAD, mirroring the cut the loop brace already does at a tick discontinuity; a note sounding when the main thread stalls is released at the re-anchor instead of sustaining for the whole stall. New test in transport.test.ts: 'releases a note that was sounding when the stall began' (note-off must land at 2.1 + START_LEAD, not a stall-length later). Verified it fails when the cutSounding call is removed.

MAJOR (SS12) src/engine/transport/clipEventSource.ts — spurious unpaired note-offs when a look-ahead window boundary fell on a clip-loop repetition boundary after a jump. beginWindow now snapshots seg/orphanCutoff and restores the cutoff when the window continues the previous one (!jumped) and the boundary back-up lands back in the repetition the cursor was already in; enterSegment still retires the cutoff for genuine forward motion into a new repetition. Two new tests in clipEventSource.test.ts: the finding's exact repro (length 2000, loop {100,800}) and a differential over every split point of a post-jump range. Both fail without the fix.

MAJOR (SS15 / SS18-M0) src/demo/engine.test.ts — the chain assembly now has coverage. Added an audioPaths() walk over the fake nodes' recorded connections and asserted that at least one audio path runs from the synth worklet node to the destination and that EVERY such path passes through the one FakeBiquadNode (plus that the filter itself reaches the destination). Mutation-verified: replacing the two wiring lines in src/demo/engine.ts with synth.output.connect(destination) now fails this test, where previously the whole suite passed.

minor (SS8) src/engine/transport/transport.ts — the loop brace is normalized to integer ticks. New normalizeLoop() rounds start/end for both deps.loop and setLoop(), the same defensive rounding play()/seek() already do, so a fractional brace can no longer throw out of the clock subscriber (dev) or seed fractional ticks into the cursor/anchor ring (prod). New test: 'rounds a fractional loop brace instead of throwing mid-tick'; fails when normalizeLoop stops rounding.

minor (SS12) src/engine/transport/transport.ts — onTick's multi-pass loop now re-checks state after each scheduleWindow (if (stateIsStopped(state)) return;), so a WindowFiller or resolveTarget that stops the transport cannot have further note-ons posted behind the panic. New test: 'stops scheduling immediately when a filler stops the transport' — asserts no noteOn appears after the allNotesOff; fails without the guard.

minor (SS7) src/devices/core/polySynth/voiceAllocator.ts — two overlapping same-pitch notes on one track now get two voices. allocate() no longer retriggers a held pitch (that branch only ever fired for the overlap case), and release() frees the OLDEST voice holding the pitch, so note-offs pair with note-ons in arrival order and the second note survives the first note-off. Doc comments cite the transport's deliberately non-deduplicated sounding ledger. voiceAllocator.test.ts's retrigger test is replaced by 'gives two overlapping notes of the same pitch two voices'.

minor (SS7) src/params/handle.ts + src/devices/harness/deviceInstance.ts — a fade scheduled in the future is no longer anchored at the value read now. writeAudioParam uses param.cancelAndHoldAtTime(at) when available (holding the value the automation really has at at) and keeps the cancelScheduledValues + setValueAtTime(param.value, at) path as the Firefox fallback. FakeAudioParam gained cancelAndHoldAtTime (recorded as a 'hold' event). New tests: deviceInstance.test.ts 'anchors a future fade at the value it will really have, not the one read now' (events are ['hold','linear'] at when) and handle.test.ts 'anchors the de-zipper ramp with cancelAndHoldAtTime when the param has it'.

minor (SS12) src/engine/context/unlock.ts + boot.ts — the unlock listeners no longer detach themselves after the first successful resume, which is what the module header always promised (a context the UA suspends later is unlocked again by the next gesture); the returned Unsub is now the only detach path, and the header/JSDoc were rewritten to say exactly that. bootAudioContext keeps the Unsub in a module-level slot and detaches the previous boot's set before arming a new one, so re-booting no longer leaks a listener set. unlock.test.ts's 'detaches all gesture listeners once the context is actually running' is replaced by 'stays armed after a successful resume, so a later suspension recovers' plus an explicit unsub test; new boot.test.ts case 'replaces the previous boot's gesture listeners instead of stacking them'.

minor (SS15 / SS4 fast path A) src/demo/offlineRender.ts + e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts — the buffer proof is no longer level-only. analyze() now also reports hfRatio (mean-square of the first difference over mean-square of the signal — a cheap monotone high-frequency measure, exactly (2 sin(pi f/fs))^2 for a sine), renderDemoOffline takes an optional cutoffHz written through the SS4 handle (setLive + commit, no new write path), and a new e2e test renders the same clip at 100 Hz and 12 kHz cutoff and asserts bright.rms > dark.rms * 4 and bright.hfRatio > dark.hfRatio * 1.3 (measured ~8x and ~1.8x). That fails if core.filter is out of the path or bound to the wrong AudioParam. New unit test in offlineRender.test.ts pins hfRatio against the closed form. Ran the full Playwright suite: 13/13 pass.

minor (SS15) src/engine/transport/transport.test.ts — prunePending(now) now has a test: 'prunes elapsed note-ons so a long playback never trips the overflow' schedules ~2900 note-ons over 3 s and asserts stop() emits exactly ONE allNotesOff (the per-note ledger), which fails as two once the prune call is deleted.

minor (SS8/SS15) src/engine/transport/transport.test.ts — the integer-tick normalization at play()/seek() now has a test: 'rounds a fractional tick handed to play() and seek()' (play(100.6) -> 101, seek(BEAT + 0.4) -> BEAT, seek(7.5) while stopped -> 8). Fails when either Math.round is removed.

minor (SS8/SS15) src/time/tempoMap.ts + src/time/dev.ts — the segment invariants createTempoMap documents now actually ship. dev.ts gained requireIntegerTicks/requirePositiveFinite (unconditional, for cold paths); assertIntegerTicks/assertPositiveFinite stay dev-only for per-event paths and delegate to them. validateSegments uses the require* pair, so a bpm of 0 or a fractional startTick throws in a production build instead of silently producing Infinity/NaN seconds. New tempoMap.test.ts describe 'what actually ships (production build)' re-imports the module with vi.stubEnv('DEV', false) + vi.resetModules and pins both halves: validation still throws, while the per-event secondsAt guard is compiled out. Mutation-verified.

minor (SS15) src/worklets/placeholder-processor.ts — corrected the stale header: it now says the URL comes from the ?worker&url suffix (not plain ?url) and points at src/engine/context/audioContext.ts as the single authoritative account of that build decision, plus at src/devices/core/polySynth.ts as the device-side example.

rejected.finding: panic() sends allNotesOff only to seenTracks, not literally 'every track' (SS12)
rejected.reason: Not fixable without changing a frozen contract, and not a defect today. TransportDeps.resolveTarget is a lookup (ChannelId -> NoteTarget | undefined) with no way to enumerate channels, so 'every channel the resolver can produce' would require adding an enumerator to the frozen TransportDeps — a contract change with no M0 caller. The reviewer agrees it is behaviourally equivalent in M0 (one track, and every note reaching an instrument goes through scheduleWindow, which is what populates seenTracks). I documented the boundary in place instead: the loop in panic() now carries a comment stating the equivalence condition, and that widening belongs with the first non-scheduler note source (SS12's count-in click, MIDI-input capture).

rejected.finding: SS12's 'ring buffers for messages' is unimplemented — each note event is a structured-cloned port.postMessage, so the audio render thread allocates one object per event
rejected.reason: Knowingly deferred, and out of proportion to M0. Removing that allocation means a SharedArrayBuffer ring with a lock-free write/read protocol, a worklet-side reader replacing port.onmessage, and a fallback for contexts where SAB is unavailable — new audio-thread machinery, i.e. exactly the kind of change a round-3 fix pass should not land untested against real hardware. src/devices/core/polySynth.ts already documents the split honestly (main-thread half done with one reused payload per message type; the receiving allocation belongs to the platform's structured clone, the COOP/COEP headers for a ring are already in place, the ring lands with the SS6 metering work). The processor copies each event into its preallocated typed-array queue and retains nothing, so the deserialized object dies young and nothing else on the render thread allocates per event. Left as-is, unchanged.

findings.description: §12 says "Stop sends allNotesOff(now + ε) down every track". `panic()` (line ~470) instead iterates `seenTracks`, i.e. only the tracks on which THIS playback pass actually scheduled a note (`beginPlayback` clears the list). The code documents the narrowing and it is equivalent for M0's single hard-coded track, but it is a literal divergence from the cited requirement and silently becomes wrong for the two other note sources §12 itself names (the metronome/count-in click instrument on a hidden channel, and record-mode MIDI input): a voice put into an instrument by anything other than the scheduler is never reached by the stop panic, because `NoteTargetResolver` has no enumerator and nothing else registers the channel as 'seen'.

The `type` param is bound through fast path B (`messageParams`), whose contract in §4/`ParamHandle.bindMessage` is `fn(v: number, when: Seconds)` with `when` in audio-clock seconds. The binding at line ~52 declares `(value: number) => { filter.type = filterTypeFromIndex(value) }` and drops `when` entirely, so a write timestamped for a future instant is applied at the next render quantum instead of at `when`. Benign in M0 (the only writes are the bind-time push and UI gestures at `currentTime`), but with the 200 ms look-ahead an §11 automation write would land up to a full look-ahead window early. `BiquadFilterNode.type` genuinely has no scheduling primitive, so the fix is a note in the contract or a scheduled-apply shim, not a one-liner.

`createAudioContext` unconditionally `await`s `audioWorklet.addModule(placeholderWorkletUrl)` on every boot of the shipped app, so the production bundle ships and loads a do-nothing silent processor (`src/worklets/placeholder-processor.ts`) purely as scaffolding; §15's worklet-bundling seam is now proved for real by `core.poly-synth`'s own `prepare()`. Relatedly, `src/workers/placeholder.worker.ts` is referenced by nothing (only mentioned in a comment) and is absent from the build output — dead scaffolding left in src/. Neither breaks a requirement; both are M0 seeds that have outlived their purpose.

findings.planSection: SS7 ("Removal is the reverse, gain-ramped")
findings.description: Audio-clock fade reconciled with a wall-clock timer. `rampOutAndDisconnect` schedules the fade on the audio clock (`writeAudioParam(gain.gain, 0, at, rampMs)`, line 279) but schedules the follow-up `disconnect()` with `setTimeout` (line 284-289: `waitMs = (at - now)*1000 + rampMs + DISCONNECT_SLACK_MS`). The same pattern is in host.ts:139 for the port nodes. The two clocks diverge whenever `ctx.currentTime` is not advancing at wall-clock rate — a UA-suspended context in a backgrounded tab, a context that never unlocked, or an `OfflineAudioContext` (already reachable in M0 via `renderDemoOffline`). The nodes are then hard-disconnected before the ramp has run at all, which is precisely the un-ramped cut the ramp exists to prevent. Secondly, the two waits are only ordered by coincidence: the host cuts the ports at `teardownRampMs*2` (40 ms) while the device's own fade finishes at `rampMs + 30` (50 ms); a device that passes `rampMs > 2*teardownRampMs` gets its ports disconnected mid-fade. Not reachable from M0's UI (nothing ever unmounts a device), but this is the shared harness code M2's reconciler runs on every device swap.

findings.planSection: SS12 ("Stop sends allNotesOff(now + e) down every track")
findings.description: `panic()`'s pending-overflow fallback (line 475: `if (pendingOverflowed) target?.allNotesOff(at + lookAhead)`) is emitted from `seek()` (line 584) and `setTempoMap()` (line 597) as well as from `stop()`. Both of those immediately re-anchor and schedule a fresh look-ahead window; the queued panic then lands ~200 ms into the *new* playback and releases every voice sounding at that instant — audible as playback cutting out shortly after a seek. The fallback only makes sense for `stop()`, where nothing is scheduled behind it. Requires the `PENDING_CAPACITY` (1024) ring to have overflowed inside one 200 ms window, i.e. ~5,000 note-ons/second, so it is unreachable at SS2's 16-track/40-voice budget.

findings.planSection: SS12 (guardrails — worklet message handling)
findings.description: `codeOf` (line 42-46) maps any unrecognised message `type` to `ALL_NOTES_OFF`, so a malformed message posted to the worklet port reaches the audio thread as a panic. It degrades badly: `cancelFrom(undefined)` is a silent no-op because `x >= undefined` is always false (line 113), and `pendWhen[i] = event.when` stores `undefined` -> `NaN`, which `sampleOffsetForBlock` maps to offset 0 (scheduling.ts, `if (!Number.isFinite(when)) return 0`). Net effect: an unknown message releases every voice at the top of the very next render quantum. No M0 caller can send one (polySynth.ts posts three preallocated, well-formed payloads), so this is robustness-only — but the processor's `port.onmessage` is an untrusted boundary in the same sense the clock worker's `asCommand` narrowing already treats its own input as untrusted.

findings.planSection: SS12 (transport state machine)
findings.description: `stop()` (lines 569-576) is missing the re-entrancy guard that `beginPlayback()` (line 502/504) and the scheduling loop (line 436) both carry. It calls `panic(ctx.currentTime)` — which calls out to the caller-supplied `resolveTarget` and to `NoteTarget` methods — before `clearAnchors()` and `setState("stopped")`. If any of that callee code re-enters `play()`, the re-entrant `beginPlayback` starts the clock and pushes anchors, and then `stop()` resumes and wipes those anchors and forces `state` back to `"stopped"`: the worker clock now ticks forever at 25 ms into an `onTick` that returns immediately at line 378, and `positionTicks()` reports the parked tick. Pathological (M0's `resolveTarget` is a pure lookup), but the guard is one line and the codebase already applies it in the two comparable places.

findings.planSection: SS12 ("zero allocation in per-tick paths")
findings.description: The zero-allocation guardrail is documented on `NoteEvent` only ("ALLOCATION CONTRACT ... a source may yield the same mutable object repeatedly", lines ~38-44) and says nothing about the iterable/iterator returned by `NoteEventSource.eventsInRange`. But the transport's inner loop is `for (const ev of events.eventsInRange(fromTick, toTick))` (transport.ts:345), so the iterator and its `IteratorResult` are just as much a per-tick allocation as the event. M0's `clipEventSource` happens to preallocate all three (clipEventSource.ts:313-358) and my heap probe confirms the tick path retains nothing, but the obvious way to write the next `NoteEventSource` — a `function*` generator — allocates a generator object per window plus a result object per event, and neither the type, the doc comment, nor any test would catch it. The contract should say the iterable/iterator may also be reused and must not allocate.

findings.planSection: SS12 (transport lifecycle)
findings.description: The shipped app never calls `engine.dispose()`. `handleBoot` stores the engine in `engineRef` (line 51) and the only `useEffect` cleanup (lines 78-84) unsubscribes the cutoff `onChange` handle; the unmount path leaves the transport's worker clock ticking every 25 ms, the `AudioContext` open, and the worklet nodes connected to `destination`. The `onStateChange` subscription (line 50) is likewise never unsubscribed, so the React state setter is retained after unmount. `DemoEngine.dispose()` exists and does the right thing (engine.ts:157-162) — it is simply never wired to the component lifecycle.

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport & scheduling) — "the event iterator walks clips in tick order"; the NoteTarget pairing invariant this file's own `orphanCutoff` machinery exists to uphold
findings.description:
`beginWindow` infers "this is a jump, re-arm orphan suppression" purely from `const jumped = fromTick !== p.lastToTick;`. A `seek()` (or `setTempoMap()`) whose target tick happens to EQUAL the previous window's `toTick` is therefore treated as a contiguous continuation — even though `transport.seek()` has already called `panic()`, sent `allNotesOff`, and zeroed `soundingCount`. The source then emits the note-off of a note whose note-on it skipped, i.e. exactly the orphan note-off the whole `orphanCutoff` mechanism is written to prevent.

Deterministic repro (headless, no browser): clip at start 0, length 8*PPQ, notes A = {start 0, dur 6*PPQ, pitch 60} and B = {start 2*PPQ, dur 5*PPQ, pitch 60}; tempo 120, lookAhead 0.2. `play(0)` schedules window [0, 374) (374 = ticksAt(0.195)). Then `seek(374)` — which lands exactly on `lastToTick`. The resulting NoteTarget call stream is:
  on 60 @0.0050, off 60 @0.0100, all @0.0050,   <- play + panic
  on 60 @0.8102,                                 <- B
  off 60 @2.8102,                                <- A's note-off, ORPHAN (A's note-on was never delivered on this pass)
  off 60 @3.3102                                 <- B's real note-off
One note-on, two note-offs. On the audio thread `VoiceAllocator.release(60)` matches the orphan off @2.8102 to B's live voice, so B is cut 0.5 s short and its own off @3.3102 releases nothing. The bug is the inference itself: a seek/tempo-change is a discontinuity regardless of which tick it lands on, and the transport never tells the source so. Probability per arbitrary seek is roughly 1/(window width in ticks) ≈ 0.5% at the default look-ahead, and M1's playhead scrubbing will exercise it constantly.

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport & scheduling) — "jitter in the tick loop never reaches the audio"
findings.description:
The stall re-anchor branch in `onTick` (`if (cursorTime < now) { ... cutSounding(cursorTime); pushAnchor(...) }`) releases every held note, but the re-anchor is a discontinuity in TIME only — the tick stream stays contiguous, so `clipEventSource` never learns about it and later emits those same notes' note-offs. The in-code comment claims "Its (late) note-off still arrives and finds nothing to release, which is the same no-op an already-released voice gets after the brace's cut." That claim is false: the brace cut is paired with the source's `orphanCutoff` suppression, the re-anchor cut is not.

Repro: clip length 8*PPQ with two overlapping same-pitch notes A = {start 0, dur 4*PPQ, pitch 60} and B = {start 2*PPQ, dur 4*PPQ, pitch 60} (a case the codebase explicitly commits to supporting — see the `markSounding` ledger comment here and the `VoiceAllocator.allocate` doc). Play from 0, then simulate a 700 ms main-thread stall (ctx.currentTime = 0.7, one tick). Emitted stream: on60@0.0050, off60@0.7050 (the cut), on60@1.5102 (B), off60@2.5102 (A's stale off), off60@3.5102 (B's off). Replaying that through the shipped `VoiceAllocator`: the off@2.5102 releases B's voice (A's slot was already freed at 0.705), so B is truncated by a full second, and B's own off@3.5102 returns null. Either the transport must suppress the stale note-offs it has already answered, or the cut must not release notes the source will still close.

findings.planSection: §12 (Transport & scheduling) — the two-clock scheduling loop and its re-entrancy contract
findings.description:
`onTick`'s scheduling loop guards re-entrant `stop()` (`if (stateIsStopped(state)) return;` after `scheduleWindow`) but NOT re-entrant `seek()` / `setTempoMap()` — even though the comment immediately above that guard says the caller code "is allowed to stop or seek the transport". `seek()` calls `restartCursor(target)` and a nested `onTick()`; when control returns to the outer loop it unconditionally executes `cursorTime = endTime;` and `cursorTick = windowEnd;`, overwriting the seek with the PRE-seek window end. `setTempoMap()` has the identical shape.

Repro: 8 notes one per beat (pitches 60..67), lookAhead 0.2, a `WindowFiller` that calls `transport.seek(6*BEAT)` on its first `fillWindow`. Running the clock to t=1.2 s yields note-ons [60, 66, 61, 62]: 66 is the seek target's note, but 61 and 62 (ticks 480 and 960, well before the seek point) are then scheduled because the cursor was restored to the pre-seek position. Meanwhile `positionTicks()` reports 8054 — it follows the seek's anchor ring, which `restartCursor` did reset. So the playhead and the audio diverge permanently. M0 registers no `WindowFiller`, but `addWindowFiller` is part of the frozen `Transport` contract shipped in M0 and is exactly where §11's automation sampler attaches in M3; `resolveTarget` and the `NoteTarget` callbacks are caller code inside the same loop and hit the same hole.

findings.planSection: §12 guardrail ("resume the context on first user gesture") / §18-M0 "Context boot + unlock"
findings.description: `bootingRef` (line 34) is set to `true` at the top of `handleBoot` (line 44) and is never reset — the `finally` block only calls `setBooting(false)`. On a failed boot (e.g. `audioWorklet.addModule` rejecting on a flaky fetch, or `createDemoEngine` throwing) the catch sets status to `failed: ...`, `booting` goes false so the button re-enables via `disabled={ready || booting}`, but every subsequent click returns immediately at `if (bootingRef.current || engineRef.current) return;`. The Boot button is then permanently dead while looking clickable, and audio can only be recovered with a page reload. The synchronous double-click guard the ref exists for is only needed for the in-flight window; it needs `bootingRef.current = false` in the `finally` (or at least in the `catch`).

findings.planSection: §7 (Device system) — voice allocation behind noteOn/noteOff/allNotesOff
findings.description: Voice bookkeeping is split between the processor (`voice.pitch`) and `VoiceAllocator` (`pitches[]`), and they can desynchronise. With `sustain === 0` — reachable, `p.percent("sustain", { default: 70 })` has min 0 — `AdsrEnvelope.next()` transitions decay → `idle` while the note is still HELD (see envelope.ts: `this.stage = this.sustainLevel > 0 ? "sustain" : "idle"`). The render loop then clears `voice.pitch = null`, but nothing frees the allocator slot, which stays occupied until the note's note-off arrives. `lruFreeIndex()` consequently reports no free voice while up to all 8 slots are provably silent, and `allocate()` falls through to `oldestIndex()` (steal) instead of the free-voice path. Audible impact is small in practice (the stolen slot is usually one of the silent ones, since stamps are monotonic), but the invariant "allocator slot occupied ⇒ voice may be sounding" is broken and any future policy that trusts it — release-tail-aware stealing, voice-count metering — will be wrong.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing)
findings.description: REVIEW-ROUND CONTAMINATION, NOT M0 CODE — but it currently fails two of the three acceptance commands and must be deleted before the gate runs. Five files (probe1..probe5.test.ts, mtimes 05:54-05:58 today, i.e. written by parallel round-4 reviewers well after the newest src file at 05:33) sit inside vitest's `include` glob (`src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, vite.config.ts) and inside the tsc program. Consequences I reproduced: (a) `npx vitest run` reports `Test Files 2 failed | 33 passed, Tests 10 failed | 403 passed`; with `--exclude 'src/__probe__/**'` it is `32 passed / 373 passed`, fully green. (b) `npx playwright test` never starts — `npm run build:e2e` runs `tsc --noEmit` over the whole repo and dies with `src/__probe__/probe2.test.ts(27,7): error TS6133`, `probe4.test.ts(43,9)`, `probe5.test.ts(3,1)`, so playwright reports only `Process from config.webServer was not able to start. Exit code: 2`. That kills the entire e2e suite, including SS15's mandated OfflineAudioContext buffer proof. After building/serving manually to bypass it, all 13 e2e tests pass. Action: remove src/__probe__/ (and instruct reviewers to keep probes in the scratchpad, per the review brief).

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing)
findings.description: SS15's buffer assertions are present but too weak to detect the scheduler failure they exist to catch: the clip's later notes being dropped. The spec only requires SOME loud window in the first third and SOME loud window in the middle third, plus a quiet final window. I rendered the demo and dumped the envelope: 50 windows of 50 ms, loud mask `11111111111111111111111111111111111111111110000000`, with the 8 attacks visible as peaks at windows 5/10/15/20/25/30/35 (0.311, 0.327, 0.325, 0.355, 0.325, 0.298, 0.311). If the transport stopped opening look-ahead windows after ~1.0 s (notes 5-8 lost), windows 0-25 would still be loud — first third loud, middle third loud (mid third is windows 16-32), last window still 0 — and every assertion in the spec would still pass. `result.ticks > 10` would not catch it either, since the ManualClock keeps ticking from the suspend loop regardless of whether the transport schedules anything. A count of distinct attack peaks (>= 8), or a requirement that loud windows extend to ~window 40 (t ~ 2.0 s, the clip's end), would close it.

findings.planSection: SS15 (testing)
findings.description: The SS15 integration proof is structurally outside the default test command and nothing runs both halves together. `npm test` is `vitest run` (src only); the OfflineAudioContext render lives exclusively in `npm run test:e2e`, which additionally needs a `--mode e2e` production build and the `window.__fabletonDemo` bridge in src/main.tsx. There is no `test:all` (or equivalent) script, so the ordinary green-suite signal for this repo does not include the one test SS15 names explicitly. Related: `renderDemoOffline` (src/demo/offlineRender.ts:170-209 — the suspend/resume tick loop with its render-quantum alignment math) is the only piece of engine-adjacent logic with 0% headless coverage; only its pure `analyze` half is unit-tested. Also note playwright.config.ts sets `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`, so a local run silently asserts against whatever bundle is already on :4173 — I hit exactly this while working around the probe-file build failure.

fixed: MAJOR (clipEventSource jump inference) + MAJOR (stall re-anchor emits stale note-offs): both were the same root cause — the source had to GUESS at discontinuities. Added an additive, optional method to the frozen contract: `NoteEventSource.onDiscontinuity?(): void` (/workspaces/fableton/src/types/transport.ts). Being optional, no existing call site breaks; the one implementation (createClipEventSource) now implements it, and `beginWindow(p, from, to, forced)` uses `const jumped = forced || fromTick !== p.lastToTick` — the tick comparison survives only as a fallback. transport.ts calls the new `markDiscontinuity()` from `restartCursor` (covers play/seek/setTempoMap, including a seek landing exactly on the previous window's toTick), from the stall re-anchor beside its `cutSounding`, and from the loop-brace wrap. Regression tests added in transport.test.ts ('transport — discontinuities never emit an unpaired note-off', with an `orphanOffCount` helper that models an instrument's held-note ledger); verified both new tests FAIL when the `forced ||` is removed.

MAJOR (re-entrant seek/setTempoMap in onTick's scheduling loop): added a `cursorEpoch` counter bumped by `restartCursor` (/workspaces/fableton/src/engine/transport/transport.ts). The loop now captures it before `scheduleWindow` and bails on `stateIsStopped(state) || cursorEpoch !== epoch`, so a WindowFiller/NoteTarget/resolveTarget that seeks is no longer overwritten by `cursorTime = endTime; cursorTick = windowEnd;`. Test 'keeps the seek instead of restoring the pre-seek cursor' added; verified it fails without the epoch check (it reproduced the reported [60, 66, 61, 62] stream).

MINOR (stop() re-entrancy, SS12 state machine): `stop()` now captures `cursorEpoch` before `panic`, re-panics once if caller code restarted playback from inside it (those note-ons were scheduled BEHIND the first panic), and calls `clock.stop()` AFTER the panic rather than before — a re-entrant `beginPlayback` no longer leaves a 25 ms clock ticking while `state` reads "stopped". Stop still wins, coherently. Test: 'tears down a playback pass restarted from inside the panic'.

MINOR (panic's pending-overflow fallback fired from seek/setTempoMap): `panic(now, final)` now takes an explicit flag; the second `allNotesOff(at + lookAhead)` is emitted only from `stop()`, where nothing is scheduled behind it. `seek()`/`setTempoMap()` pass `false` (transport.ts).

MINOR (zero-allocation guardrail documented on NoteEvent only): /workspaces/fableton/src/types/transport.ts now states the allocation contract on `eventsInRange` itself — the iterable, its iterator and the yielded events may all be reused, a `function*` generator is explicitly not an acceptable implementation, and the consumer therefore gets one live iteration at a time.

MINOR (filter `type` drops bindMessage's `when`): documented at both ends rather than faked. `ParamHandle.bindMessage` (/workspaces/fableton/src/types/params.ts) now requires implementations to honour `when` and requires a binding whose target has no scheduling primitive to say so at the binding site; /workspaces/fableton/src/devices/core/filter.ts explains that the enum lands up to one look-ahead window early under SS11 automation, and why a wall-clock setTimeout shim would be worse (it drifts against ctx.currentTime the moment the context is suspended or offline).

MINOR (placeholder scaffolding, SS15): deleted src/worklets/placeholder-processor.ts and src/workers/placeholder.worker.ts. `createAudioContext` no longer loads a do-nothing processor on every boot (it is now synchronous — `bootAudioContext` was the only caller) and `PLACEHOLDER_WORKLET_URL` is gone from src/engine/context/index.ts. The authoritative `?worker&url` account moved to the seam that now owns it, `core.poly-synth`'s prepare() (src/devices/core/polySynth.ts). Updated audioContext.test.ts, boot.ts, clock.worker.ts's comment, App.tsx's comment and e2e/render/worklet-chunk.spec.ts (which still proves the emitted chunk is served with 200 and that boot awaits addModule end to end).

MINOR (audio-clock fade reconciled with a wall-clock timer): added `runAfterAudioTime(ctx, doneAt, firstWaitMs, schedule, body)` and `deviceTeardownWaitMs(rampMs)` to /workspaces/fableton/src/devices/harness/deviceInstance.ts. The wall-clock timer is now only the first guess: on waking, the AUDIO clock decides whether to cut or wait again (capped at 5 s, after which a permanently stalled — and therefore silent — context gets cut anyway, so teardown can't leak). `rampOutAndDisconnect` and host.ts's port teardown both go through it. The ordering is no longer a coincidence of two default numbers: host.ts uses `Math.max(teardownRampMs * 2, deviceTeardownWaitMs() + teardownRampMs)` (70 ms vs the device's 50 ms, where it was 40 vs 50 — i.e. ports were being cut mid-fade), and `RampOutOptions.rampMs` documents that a longer ramp needs a matching `teardownRampMs`. Tests updated to advance the fake audio clock, plus two new ones: 'does not cut the ports while the audio clock is not advancing' and 'gives up and disconnects once a stalled context has run out the budget'.

MINOR (worklet message boundary): `codeOf` in /workspaces/fableton/src/devices/core/polySynth/noteEventQueue.ts returns -1 for an unrecognised type, and `push` drops anything unrecognised or with a non-finite `when` into the `dropped` counter instead of coercing it to ALL_NOTES_OFF. Test: 'drops a malformed message instead of treating it as a panic'.

MINOR (voice/allocator desync at sustain 0): `AdsrEnvelope.next()` now moves decay -> "sustain" even at level 0 instead of -> "idle" (/workspaces/fableton/src/devices/core/polySynth/envelope.ts). A voice is idle when its NOTE is over, not when its amplitude reaches zero, so the processor no longer clears `voice.pitch` under a held note while the allocator slot stays occupied, and `allocate()` no longer steals while slots are provably silent. `noteOff` from a zero-level sustain releases and lands in `idle` on the next sample. Chose this over freeing the allocator slot from the render loop, which would have let a stale note-off release a NEWER same-pitch note that had taken the reused slot. envelope.test.ts's sustain-0 case rewritten accordingly.

MINOR (App lifecycle): /workspaces/fableton/src/app/App.tsx now unsubscribes the transport `onStateChange` handle and calls `engine.dispose()` from the unmount effect (stopping the 25 ms worker clock, disposing devices and unregistering params), and `bootingRef.current = false` moved into `handleBoot`'s `finally` so a failed boot no longer dead-ends the Boot button. Tests 'disposes the engine when the component unmounts' and 're-arms the Boot button after a failed boot'; verified the latter fails without the ref reset.

MINOR (SS15 buffer proof too weak): /workspaces/fableton/e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts now requires a loud window inside EVERY one of the clip's eight note slots (slot bounds derived from `result.durationSeconds` / `windowRms.length`, so nothing is hard-coded to the window size), replacing the 'something loud in the first third, something in the middle third' pair that a scheduler dropping notes 5-8 would still have passed. The quiet-final-window assertion is kept.

MINOR (SS15 integration proof outside the default command): added `"test:all": "npm run test && npm run test:e2e"` to package.json, and set `reuseExistingServer: false` in playwright.config.ts — this suite asserts against the built bundle (it reads dist/assets and needs the `--mode e2e` bridge), so a stale server on :4173 was being silently asserted against; with `strictPort` a leftover server now fails loudly instead.

rejected.finding: MINOR — `panic()` iterates `seenTracks` rather than 'every track', diverging literally from SS12's "Stop sends allNotesOff(now + ε) down every track"
rejected.reason: Cannot be fixed without growing a frozen contract, and nothing in M0 needs it. `TransportDeps.resolveTarget` is a `NoteTargetResolver` — a lookup with no enumerator — so 'every channel that exists' is not knowable from inside the transport; widening it means adding an enumeration method to the frozen TransportDeps/NoteTargetResolver contract with no caller that benefits. The reviewer's own two motivating cases (the metronome/count-in click instrument and record-mode MIDI input) do not exist in M0, and while the scheduler is the only thing that can put a note into an instrument the two sets are identical. The narrowing is already documented at the call site together with the exact trigger for revisiting it (the first non-scheduler note source), which is where the enumerator should land.

rejected.finding: MINOR — src/__probe__/probe1..5.test.ts contaminate the acceptance commands
rejected.reason: Already resolved before this round: `src/__probe__` does not exist in the working tree (`ls src/` shows app, demo, devices, engine, main.tsx, params, time, types, workers, worklets). Nothing to delete. Confirmed by the acceptance commands themselves: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0, `npx vitest run` is 32 files / 382 tests green, and `npx playwright test` runs its full 13 tests (they were previously blocked by TS6133 errors in those probe files).

rejected.finding: MINOR (sub-point of the package.json finding) — `renderDemoOffline`'s suspend/resume tick loop has 0% headless coverage
rejected.reason: Not fixable in the unit suite as it stands: the loop's whole subject is a real `OfflineAudioContext` with render-quantum-aligned `suspend()` promises, and vitest's jsdom environment ships no Web Audio implementation at all (the reason the module's header says it only runs in a browser). Faking it would test the fake. It IS covered — by e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts, whose assertions this round strengthened, and that suite is now reachable from a single command (`npm run test:all`), which was the actionable half of the finding.

result.summary: M0's named scope is complete and green — tsc clean, 382 Vitest tests in 32 files, `vite build` OK, 13/13 Playwright specs against a production `vite preview`, and the .playwright/screenshots/M0 images show the real UI (Boot/Play/Stop, cutoff slider reading "1.00 kHz", transport "playing"). Verified present and tested: ParamRegistry with hierarchical `chan:/dev:/leaf` ids, real-unit values with clamp-on-load, taper boundary, free/automated/overridden, bindAudioParam + bindMessage + rAF-coalesced onChange; the SS7 device harness (prepare/create/register/connectParam, gain-ramped removal, gainParams/scaledParams/msParam covering the SS14 playbook shape verbatim); PolySynth (worklet, 8 voices, sample-accurate note starts) and Filter; the SS12 transport (25 ms worker clock, 200 ms horizon raised to a floor, tempo-map-only tick↔seconds, loop brace, stall re-anchor, orphan-note-off suppression, allNotesOff on stop) with an unusually thorough 1156-line test; the 960-PPQ TempoMap; and the browser proofs (AnalyserNode RMS on boot→play→stop, OfflineAudioContext render with per-note energy and a cutoff-vs-spectrum check, worklet chunk served 200, zero console/page/network errors). No blockers found. The gaps below are all things the milestone can pass its gate without, but that are either §-text with no implementation, or shipped behavior with no test guarding it.

gaps.description: Nothing verifies, in a browser, that the shipped app's 25 ms clock actually runs in a dedicated Worker — the single property SS12 chose a Worker for ("main-thread timers throttle in background tabs"). src/engine/transport/clock.ts's createDefaultClock() try/catches Worker construction and silently returns createTimerClock() (main-thread setInterval); on a platform without module workers the app would degrade to exactly the throttled timer SS12 rejects and every test would still pass. e2e/interaction/transport.spec.ts only proves *some* clock keeps opening windows; it cannot tell the two apart, and no test backgrounds/hides the tab to prove ticks survive throttling. The build emits dist/assets/clock.worker-*.js, but e2e/render/worklet-chunk.spec.ts filters chunks with /-processor-.*\.js$/, so the clock worker chunk is the one emitted entry point never asserted to serve 200. Both halves of the protocol are well unit-tested against a FakeWorker (clock.test.ts), which is precisely why the real-Worker path is the untested one.

"Zero allocation in per-tick paths" is honored by construction throughout transport.ts (typed-array rings, index loops, cached target lookup) and is tested where an object is reused — clipEventSource.test.ts "reuses one event object (SS12 allocation contract)" and polySynth.test.ts "reuses one payload object per message type" — but nothing tests the transport's own tick path (onTick / scheduleWindow / panic / prunePending). A regression such as a `for...of` over `fillers`/`stateListeners`, or a closure created per window, would allocate on every tick at 40 Hz and pass the entire suite.

SS12: "Metronome and count-in are scheduled like any other events, targeting a built-in click instrument on a hidden channel." Neither exists — no click device, no hidden channel, no count-in state on the transport. The only trace is a comment in transport.ts:514 noting that widening panic() beyond `seenTracks` would need an enumerator once a non-scheduler note source ("SS12's count-in click") arrives. Not named in the SS18-M0 bullet and the hidden-channel notion depends on the M2 channel model, so this is deferred rather than broken — but it is unimplemented SS12 text with no seam.

SS12's `stopped → playing → recording` is only half-exposed: `record()` lives on the local EngineTransport interface (src/engine/transport/transport.ts), not on the frozen `Transport` contract in src/types/transport.ts, so nothing holding a `Transport` can reach the recording state. There is also no capture flag beyond the state string and no UI path (App.tsx has Boot/Play/Stop only). Unit-tested at transport.test.ts:169 ("record() is playing plus a capture flag"), so this is a contract/reachability gap, not a behavioral one.

None of SS7's five swap steps are implemented: no parallel muted create, no allNotesOff-then-~20 ms crossfade swap path, no param carry-over by matching local id and range, no keep-and-grey of automation lanes. The primitives exist and are tested individually (DEFAULT_RAMP_OUT_MS = 20 ms, rampOutAndDisconnect, harness-owned port nodes that survive an instance, host.mount/unmount), and the transport already re-resolves each track's instrument per tick (transport.test.ts:844) so the scheduler side is ready — but there is no swap function and no test of a swap. Reasonable to land with the M2 reconciler; listed because SS7 is a cited M0 detail section.

`migrateParams(old, fromVersion)` is declared on DeviceDefinition (src/types/devices.ts) and `version` is validated at registration (integer >= 1, and re-registering a different definition under a live id throws), but migrateParams is never invoked anywhere in the codebase, there is no helper that applies it on load, and no test exercises a migration. SS7 calls param local-ids "public API: renaming one requires a migration" — that contract currently has no runtime or test behind it. Project load/save arrives in M1, so this is deferral rather than divergence.

gaps.area: devices + UI — declarative panels and the SS5 gesture spec
gaps.description: `PanelSpec`/`PanelRowSpec`/`PanelControlSpec` are declared in src/types/devices.ts and the registry validates that a panel only references declared param ids (registry.ts), but nothing renders a panel and neither core device declares one, so SS7's "omit → auto-generated (SS5)" path does not exist yet. M0's single live control is a raw `<input type=range>` in App.tsx: it follows none of the SS5 gesture table (relative drag with 150 px = full sweep, no jump-to-click-point, shift-fine with mid-drag re-anchor, hidden cursor, floating readout, double-click reset, type-in via fromText). fromText is implemented and tested on every descriptor factory but is unreachable from the UI. The control kit is M2 scope; flagged so it is a known deferral rather than an assumed one.

gaps.area: time — tick integrality of clip/note data
gaps.description: SS8's "always integer" is enforced only inside src/time/ — src/time/dev.ts is explicitly documented as "not part of the public API — used only inside src/time/", and its guards fire in createTempoMap, TempoMap.secondsAt/bpmAt and grid.ts. The transport defensively rounds its own entry points (play/seek/setLoop). But nothing validates MidiClip.start/length, Note.start/dur or clip loop bounds: createClipEventSource filters only `muted !== true && dur >= 1 && start >= 0`, and the sort/lowerBound/tiling math would accept fractional ticks. A fractional Note.start therefore reaches tempoMap.secondsAt and throws in dev but is silently converted in a production build — the reverse of the intended fail-loud-early behavior.

gaps.area: build — the shipped bundle is never exercised
gaps.description: playwright.config.ts's webServer always runs `npm run build:e2e` (`--mode e2e`), so every browser test asserts against a bundle that is not the shipped one. src/main.tsx claims the e2e bridge "must not ship" and relies on `import.meta.env.MODE === "e2e"` being statically replaced; that claim has no test. (I verified it manually: a plain `vite build` produces a bundle containing no `__fabletonDemo` and no `renderDemoOffline`/`OfflineAudioContext` reference, while the e2e bundle does — so the guard works today, but a regression that leaks the live ParamRegistry and EngineTransport onto `window` in production would not fail anything.) Nothing loads the production build at all, so its zero-console-error property is likewise unasserted.

gaps.area: tests — the OfflineAudioContext buffer proof is not in `vitest run`
gaps.description: SS15 says the engine runs headless against OfflineAudioContext in integration tests and "no browser needed for any of the load-bearing logic". The render-and-assert-on-buffer proof exists and is strong, but it lives in e2e/audio/offline-render.spec.ts and needs Playwright + Chromium: src/demo/offlineRender.ts is browser-only (jsdom has no Web Audio) and its Vitest companion covers only `analyze()`'s arithmetic against stub buffers. Consequence: `npm test` on its own contains no sample-level proof that the spine makes sound — that requires `npm run test:all`. The reason is documented in the file headers and headless Chromium is a defensible reading of "headless", so this is a noted divergence rather than a missing test.

gaps.area: demo/e2e — loop brace, seek and clip-loop unrolling have no end-to-end proof
gaps.description: Transport loop-brace behavior (wrap, note-cut at the brace, position clamping, setLoop(null), sub-tick braces) and seek-while-playing are covered exhaustively in transport.test.ts against a ManualClock and fakes, and clip-loop unrolling is covered in clipEventSource.test.ts — but none of it ever runs through real audio: DEMO_CLIP has no `loop`, createDemoEngine passes no LoopRegion, and App.tsx exposes only Play/Stop. So the only paths proved against rendered samples or a live AudioContext are linear one-shot playback and stop. An error confined to the loop/seek path in the real (non-manual-clock) regime would not be caught by any browser or buffer-level test.

fixed: engine/transport — worker clock (SS12): made the Worker-vs-timer choice observable and asserted it in a real browser. src/engine/transport/clock.ts now tags every clock with a `ClockKind` ("worker" | "timer" | "manual"), and `createDefaultClock`'s fallback is no longer silent — it `console.warn`s that it degraded to a main-thread timer that browsers throttle to >=1 s in background tabs (the exact failure SS12 moved the clock off the main thread to avoid). src/engine/transport/manualClock.ts tags itself "manual"; src/engine/transport/index.ts exports `ClockKind`.

src/engine/transport/transport.ts: `EngineTransport` exposes `clockKind` (reads `clock.kind`), so the shipped app's degradation is observable from outside the engine — this is what the e2e bridge (src/main.tsx → `window.__fabletonDemo.engine.transport`) reads.

e2e/interaction/clock-worker.spec.ts (new, 3 tests against the production build): (1) after boot, a real dedicated Worker running the clock module exists in `page.workers()` AND the live transport reports `clockKind === "worker"` — a silent fallback to `createTimerClock` now fails the suite; (2) tick provenance — `self.postMessage` is wrapped inside the worker's own global scope to count posts, and after Stop the look-ahead window count is asserted <= worker tick posts + 1 (the one window `play()` fills synchronously), so nothing but worker-posted ticks can be driving the scheduler; (3) the tick timer keeps firing while the page's main thread is hard-blocked for 600 ms (>=12 ticks posted, where a coalesced main-thread `setInterval` manages ~1). Verified negatively: with `createDefaultClock` forced to return `createTimerClock`, all three fail (with a diagnostic naming the observed `clockKind`).

e2e/render/worker-chunk.spec.ts (new): the emitted `dist/assets/clock.worker-*.js` chunk — previously the one built entry point never asserted — is served 200 with a JavaScript content-type (an SPA HTML fallback would 200 and still fail to instantiate as a module worker). Mirrors e2e/render/worklet-chunk.spec.ts, whose `/-processor-.*\.js$/` filter skipped it.

src/engine/transport/clock.test.ts: unit coverage for the new tag and the announced fallback — each implementation reports its `kind`, and `createDefaultClock` under a Worker constructor that throws returns kind "timer" AND warns once about background-tab throttling. src/engine/transport/transport.test.ts: transport reports the injected clock's kind.

Comment accuracy: e2e/interaction/transport.spec.ts's window-filler test no longer claims to prove the worker clock (it proves *a* clock ticks) and points at the new spec; src/main.tsx's bridge comment does the same.

rejected.finding: "no test backgrounds/hides the tab to prove ticks survive throttling" — the literal hidden-tab test
rejected.reason: Not stageable in this harness, so it would have been a test that can only false-pass. Headless Chromium reports document.visibilityState === "visible" for every page it opens: a second tab brought to the front does not background the first (tried in both the default headless shell and channel: "chromium", with --disable-background-timer-throttling / --disable-renderer-backgrounding / --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows removed via ignoreDefaultArgs — the poll for "hidden" times out), and CDP has no visibility override (Page.setWebLifecycleState rejects "hidden" as an "Unidentified lifecycle state", and its "frozen" state halts the main thread's task queue outright rather than throttling timers, so it models nothing). On top of that, Chromium exempts audibly-playing pages from background throttling, so even a genuinely hidden tab would keep a main-thread timer running here and the test would pass against the fallback clock. Replaced by test (3) in e2e/interaction/clock-worker.spec.ts, which measures the same distinction from the other side and does fail against the fallback: the worker's timer keeps firing at 25 ms through a 600 ms main-thread block, where a main-thread setInterval fires once, coalesced. The rationale and the failed approaches are recorded in the spec's header comment so this isn't rediscovered later.

result.summary: Re-check after gap fixes: I re-read PLAN.md SS3/SS4/SS7/SS8/SS12/SS14/SS15/SS18-M0 and swept the whole tree (src ~6.1k lines, e2e, config), then re-ran the toolchain myself: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx vitest run` 386/386 green in 32 files, `npx vite build` succeeds emitting the worklet and clock-worker as their own chunks, `npx playwright test` 17/17 green against the production preview, and the M0 screenshots under .playwright/screenshots/M0/ regenerate and show the real mounted UI (Boot/Play/Stop, cutoff slider reading "1.00 kHz", transport state "playing"). Every named M0 deliverable is implemented AND tested: context boot with latencyHint "interactive" + gesture unlock (src/engine/context/*), ParamRegistry with hierarchical ids, tapers, real-unit values with clamp-on-load, base/live/setLive/commit, both fast paths and the free/automated/overridden machine (src/params/*), core.poly-synth (worklet + voice allocator) and core.filter as definitions on the SS7 harness with p.* factories (src/devices/*), the 25 ms worker clock + 200 ms look-ahead transport with TempoMap-only tick↔seconds and allNotesOff-on-stop (src/engine/transport/*), and the hard-coded clip audible end to end, proved numerically both in-page (AnalyserNode RMS across the phrase, no note attacking after Stop, decay to silence) and via a real OfflineAudioContext render asserting energy in every one of the eight note slots plus a cutoff-driven spectral difference. result.summary: Wrote real, pixel-verifying Playwright specs for every requested check (drag-move/resize/alt-dup, marquee, Esc-cancel, undo/redo-as-one-entry, keyboard map, Ctrl+wheel zoom-at-cursor, OPFS save/reload) against a production `vite preview` build, driving the piano roll purely through real pointer/keyboard events and reading results back off the actual rendered canvas pixels (no src/ state hooks — see e2e/interaction/editing-helpers.ts for why). Every one of them failed at the same first step: opening a clip into the piano roll (or creating a note) requires a double-click, and I found and independently confirmed a real, reproducible defect that makes every double-click-gated gesture in the app unreachable in any standards-compliant browser (Chromium verified directly): `src/editor/kit/points.ts`'s `pointerInputOf` computes `clickCount` from `PointerEvent.detail`, but `PointerEvent.detail` is spec-mandated to always be `0` (confirmed empirically: the same click sequence's native `mousedown`/`click` events correctly report `detail=1` then `detail=2`, while the `pointerdown` events the app actually listens to report `detail=0` both times). Since `clickCount` can therefore never reach 2, SS10's "dbl-click empty: create grid-length note", the arrangement's "double-click opens the piano roll" (SS18-M1), and "double-click empty track: create clip" are all dead code paths — a real user can never open ANY clip into the piano roll editor, so the entire M1 note-editing surface is unreachable through the shipped UI. I independently found and corroborated this via direct browser instrumentation before noticing the concurrent render-probe session had documented the identical root cause in e2e/render/piano-roll-open.spec.ts, which is strong independent confirmation this is real and not a fluke of my test technique. Given this, none of the 7 requested behaviors could be exercised end-to-end through genuine interaction; I did not hack around it with synthetic clickCount injection, since that would test a hypothetical fixed app rather than the real one. The specs are left on disk, correctly written against the intended behavior, and will pass once the root cause is fixed (no changes needed to the tests themselves). A second, independent gap: even if double-click worked, there is no UI control anywhere (Toolbar.tsx has no tool switcher) to put the piano roll in "pencil" mode, so SS10's drag-to-extend note creation (the Paint FSM row) has no UI entry point either — only the double-click-fixed-length path does.

result.summary: Ran the M1 render probe against a production build (`vite build --mode e2e` + `vite preview`) served through the existing `playwright.config.ts` harness (untouched — it already worked). Wrote 4 new spec files under e2e/render/ and extended e2e/render/helpers.ts with fast in-browser pixel-sampling helpers (a naive whole-canvas getImageData→JSON transfer blew the 30s test timeout on a ~2 megapixel DPR-2 canvas, so counting/scanning now happens inside page.evaluate and only small numbers cross the wire). All 13 new/existing render specs pass except one, which is intentionally red: it documents a real, reproducible M1 defect (see findings) rather than a test bug — verified via two independent signals (zero note-fill pixels in the piano roll's content canvas, and Undo staying disabled after select-all+nudge) plus a control test proving the double-click input itself is fine at the browser level. Both editors mount and render simultaneously (M1's split layout); the arrangement view shows real content (the starter clip with note-preview glyphs) and was verified to actually change (clip footprint >1.5x wider) across two zoom levels, screenshotted and eyeballed. The piano roll's grid/rows/ruler render structurally and its zoom was verified via row-band pixel-run growth, but it can never show real note content in this build because double-click (the only way to open a clip or create a note) is unreachable — see the blocker finding. DPR canvas sizing (canvas.width === round(cssWidth*dpr)) holds for every layer in both editors, and a grid hairline was proven crisp (≤3 contiguous device pixels, hard-edged) via real pixel sampling, not a code read. The SS9 playhead contract was verified end to end: a DOM div moved via transform:translateX() in both editors, its transform demonstrably changes during ~600ms of real playback, and CanvasRenderingContext2D.clearRect call counts for every grid/content/overlay layer canvas are unchanged across that same window (instrumented via a prototype patch installed before the app's module graph runs).

findings.description: pointerInputOf() derives its clickCount from `event.detail` on a native PointerEvent (`clickCount: event.detail === 0 ? 1 : event.detail`), but real browsers report `detail === 0` on every pointerdown/pointerup regardless of click count — click-count semantics exist only on MouseEvent click/dblclick, never on PointerEvent. Since gestureEngine.ts listens exclusively for pointerdown/pointerup, clickCount can NEVER reach 2 in a real browser, so every `info.clickCount >= 2` branch is dead code in production: double-clicking a clip never opens the piano roll (dragMove.ts), double-clicking an empty track header never creates a clip (dragCreate.ts), and double-clicking empty piano-roll grid never creates a note (dragMarquee.ts). This is SS10's 'Gesture FSM' contract (dbl-click open/create) and SS18-M1's stated wiring ('double-click opens the piano roll on this clip', arrangement.ts comment). Proven in the browser (not inferred) via e2e/render/piano-roll-open.spec.ts: a native `dblclick` DOM event fires correctly for the same input while every captured `pointerdown.detail` is 0, and after the double-click the piano roll's content canvas has zero note-fill pixels and Undo stays disabled after select-all+nudge (no command was ever dispatched, because no clip was ever open). The kit's own unit tests never catch this because they hand-construct PointerInput objects with `clickCount: 2` directly, bypassing pointerInputOf and real PointerEvents entirely (see arrangement.test.ts 'opens the piano roll on a double-clicked clip').
