findings.description: `pointerInputOf` derives click count as `clickCount: event.detail === 0 ? 1 : event.detail` (line 107). Real browsers report `PointerEvent.detail === 0` on EVERY pointerdown/pointerup, and the engine binds pointer events exclusively (gestureEngine.ts addEventListener("pointerdown"/"pointerup")), so `GestureStart.clickCount`/`ClickInfo.clickCount` can never exceed 1 in the shipped app. Every `clickCount >= 2` branch is therefore dead code: piano-roll double-click-empty → grid-length note (src/editor/pianoroll/dragMarquee.ts:119), arrangement double-click empty lane → one-bar clip (src/editor/arrangement/dragCreate.ts:111), and arrangement double-click clip → open piano roll (src/editor/arrangement/dragMove.ts:100). The last one is fatal: `context.openClip` is called from exactly one place, and `onOpenClip={setOpenClipId}` (src/app/App.tsx:337) is the ONLY writer of `openClipId`, so no clip can ever be opened into the piano roll — the whole §10 editor is unreachable in the running app. Substantiated in a real browser: `npx playwright test --project=chromium` → 13 failures, every one of them this root cause (all 9 piano-roll-editing specs fail at "double-click on empty grid should create exactly one new note"; zoom.spec fails at "expected the double-click to have created a note"; persistence.spec fails at "the new note should have been added"; piano-roll-open.spec's control test passes, proving the browser DOES fire a native dblclick while `pointerdown.detail` is 0 on every call). The unit suite (1083 passing) misses it because both harnesses inject `clickCount` into the plain PointerInput directly and domBinding.test.ts builds its synthetic MouseEvents with `detail: 1`, so `pointerInputOf`'s mapping is never exercised with real pointer-event semantics.

findings.planSection: §10 Gesture FSM table, row `DragDup` ("Alt+body | ghosts of copies | one command: duplicate+move")
findings.description: `createDupDragHandler.update` (lines 193–233) picks between the `duplicate` and `velocity` sub-modes from `Math.abs(update.deltaPx.y) > Math.abs(update.deltaPx.x)` on the FIRST update and then sets `locked: true` forever. The first update is the one the engine feeds straight through from `promote()`, i.e. the sample at the instant the pointer crosses the 3px threshold. Consequence: SS10's `DragDup` row is unreachable for any Alt+body drag whose opening 3–4px of travel is more vertical than horizontal — including the classic "Alt+drag a note down an octave to duplicate at a new pitch", which is a pure-vertical gesture and can NEVER duplicate. Probe (headless, real harness): Alt+pointerdown on n1 (pitch 60, vel 100), move +1px x / +40px y, then +200px x, release → dispatched `['Set Velocity']`, note count unchanged (2), n1.vel 100 → 69. No copy is ever made and no amount of subsequent horizontal travel can recover, because `locked` is already true. §10 also scopes the velocity sub-mode to "Alt+vertical-drag on selected note bodies", not to any body under the pointer.

findings.planSection: §9 ("commits exactly one command on release") / §13 (one gesture → one history entry)
findings.description: `pointerUp` (line 331) matches only on `pointerId` and ignores `input.button` / `input.buttons`. A mouse shares one pointerId across all its buttons, so pressing and releasing the secondary button during a live left-button drag delivers a `pointerup` (button 2, buttons still 1) that the FSM treats as the release: it commits the drag at that instant and returns to `idle` while the primary button is still held. Probe: pointerdown on n1, move +60px, then `pointerUp({pointerId:1, button:2, buttons:1})` → phase `idle`, `['Move Notes']` dispatched, n1 moved to tick 1200; all subsequent motion is inert and the genuine left-button release does nothing. The same hole makes a middle-click mid-drag commit the gesture. `pointerDown` guards against re-entry (`active !== null`) but the matching release guard is missing.

findings.planSection: §9 ("Every drag operates on a preview ... commits exactly one command on release") / §13
findings.description: `keyDown` (line 397) intercepts only `Escape` while a gesture is active; every other registered key binding still runs and dispatches document commands mid-drag. Probe: pointerdown on n1 → move +100px (phase `dragging`) → `Ctrl+D` → release, yields TWO commands and two history entries for one continuous gesture: `['Duplicate Notes', 'Move Notes']`. With `Delete` instead, the dragged note is deleted mid-gesture and the drag's own commit then silently degrades to null (its targets no longer resolve), so the release the user made produces no move at all. Either the FSM should suppress editor key bindings while `phase !== "idle"`, or bindings must be gesture-aware.

findings.planSection: §9 ("zoomAt keeps time under cursor fixed"; kit owns thresholds/snapping/preview)
findings.description: `buildUpdate` (line 174) derives `deltaTicks` as `viewport.tickDeltaOf(dx)` where `dx` is measured against `start.point.xPx` captured at the zoom level in force at pointerdown. `wheel()` re-runs `handler.update` after a mid-drag zoom claiming "the ghost stays under the pointer", but because the pixel anchor is stale the tick delta silently changes with no pointer motion. Probe: drag n1 +100px (preview deltaTicks 1920), then one ctrl+wheel notch (deltaY −300) at the same point → preview deltaTicks 960, ghost start jumps from 1920 to 960. Zooming or scrolling during a drag should preserve the musical delta (§9's coordinate discipline: editor logic in musical units, pixels only at the boundary); the gesture should keep its anchor in ticks/rows, not in pixels.

findings.planSection: §10 (Snapping) / §18-M1 ("full piano-roll spec (§10)")
findings.description: §10 Snapping requires "Grid is adaptive to zoom (as in Live) **with a fixed-grid override menu and a triplet toggle**". Neither exists anywhere in the product. `grid.setSettings(...)` is called ONLY from test files (`grep -rn setSettings src e2e` → src/editor/kit/grid.ts definition + 6 test files, zero production callers); the string "grid" does not appear at all in src/app/App.tsx, src/app/panels/Toolbar.tsx, ArrangementPanel.tsx or PianoRollPanel.tsx. The view API offers no post-mount escape either: `EditorViewOptionsBase.grid` (/workspaces/fableton/src/types/editor.ts:138) is a create-time-only `Partial<GridSettings>`, `EditorView`/`PianoRollView`/`ArrangementView` expose no `grid` handle and no `setGrid`, and neither panel passes the option. Consequence: both editors run `DEFAULT_GRID_SETTINGS` ({mode:'adaptive', triplet:false}) for the life of the app — a user can never pin a fixed division and can never enter triplet material, i.e. the grid half of §10's snapping spec is unimplemented at the product level even though src/editor/kit/grid.ts implements the model correctly.

findings.planSection: §10 (Gesture FSM — `Paint` row; Hit zones — "note creation in pencil mode")
findings.description: The `Paint` FSM row and the pencil hit-zone branch are implemented (src/editor/pianoroll/dragPaint.ts, hits.ts:185) but are unreachable in the shipped app. `PianoRollView.setTool` is called from exactly one production site, src/app/panels/PianoRollPanel.tsx:79, and only `if (tool !== undefined)`; App.tsx mounts `<PianoRollPanel …/>` (line ~340) without a `tool` prop, so `options.tool ?? "select"` (src/editor/pianoroll/pianoRoll.ts:130) pins the editor to select mode forever. There is no tool button in Toolbar.tsx and no key binding for it (`grep -rn "pencil" src` hits only tests, dragPaint.ts, hits.ts and the ToolMode type). So `createPaintDragHandler.claim()` — which requires `ctx.tool === "pencil"` — can never be satisfied by a real user, and the FSM's `Paint` row is dead code in the product.

findings.planSection: §10 (Gesture FSM — `DragDup` row; Hit zones — "Alt+vertical-drag on **selected** note bodies")
findings.description: `createDupDragHandler.update()` picks its sub-mode from the promoting frame — `Math.abs(update.deltaPx.y) > Math.abs(update.deltaPx.x) ? "velocity" : "duplicate"` — then sets `locked: true` for the rest of the gesture, and `claim()` never checks whether the hit note is selected. Two deviations: (a) §10 confines the Alt velocity gesture to "Alt+vertical-drag on **selected** note bodies", so on an UNSELECTED note Alt+body must be the FSM's `DragDup`; (b) because the decision is dominant-axis, `DragDup`'s "duplicate+move" can never carry a pitch change at all — an Alt-drag with any vertical dominance becomes a velocity edit. Verified with the package's own harness (probe, scratchpad): a single unselected note {start:960,dur:480,pitch:60,vel:100}, Alt-drag from the note body by (+40px x, −100px y) — an unambiguous "duplicate an octave up" gesture — dispatches `Set Velocity` and leaves one note at vel 127 (100 + round(100*126/160) clamped); no duplicate is created. A near-vertical Alt-drag (+2px, −48px) does the same. The axis lock also fires on the 3-4px promoting move, so a few pixels of jitter decide the verb for the whole gesture.

findings.planSection: §9 (Coordinate discipline — `zoomAt` "keeps time under cursor fixed"; wheel bindings)
findings.description: `setScrollRaw` rounds `scrollTicks` to an integer (`Math.round(clamp(...))`), so `zoomAt`'s anchor correction `anchor - px/next` is quantized every notch and the anchored time drifts out from under the cursor instead of staying fixed. Measured with the real module (probe): starting at pxPerTick 0.05, scrollTicks 0, 40 wheel notches of factor 1.1 anchored at x=600 leave the anchored tick at x=594 — 6 px of accumulated drift, monotonically growing as zoom increases (drift is invisible at coarse zoom, ~1px/notch near the 2 px/tick ceiling). The same rounding amplifies `scrollBy`: at pxPerTick=2, ten `scrollBy(1,0)` calls (a Shift+wheel horizontal scroll of 10 px) move the view 10 ticks = 20 px, double what was asked, and any single sub-0.25px trackpad delta rounds to 0 and is dropped. Keeping a fractional scroll origin (and rounding only in `tAt`) would satisfy the §9 contract exactly.

findings.planSection: §10 (Hit zones — "min(6 px, 40% of note width) … so short notes always keep a grabbable body")
findings.description: `noteAtPoint` widens a note's clickable span by `NOTE_HIT_SLOP_PX = 2` on each side, but `zoneOfNoteX` computes the zones against the un-widened rect, so the whole slop is absorbed by the two EDGE zones rather than by the body. The body therefore shrinks to well under the 20% of the hit target that the min(6px,40%) rule intends. Concretely, at pxPerTick=0.005 a 1/8 note is 2.4 px wide (probe output `w=2.40 edge=0.96`): the clickable span is [x−2, x+4.4] = 6.4 px, of which edge-l owns 2.96 px, edge-r owns 3.0 px and the body owns 0.48 px — ~7% of the grab area moves the note, ~93% resizes it. Zoomed-out note dragging is effectively impossible; the slop should extend the body, or the zone split should be computed over the slop-widened span.
